Interspecific variation in plant capacity to redistribute could be crucial for the reassembly of ecological communities under climate change. Abstract Climate change is causing biodiversity redistributions towards cooler areas at an unprecedented velocity. Plants are an essential component of terrestrial ecosystems that primarily rely on seed dispersal to redistribute. Yet, most seed dispersal occurs over short distances (i.e. less than 1 km), which is insufficient to track ongoing climate change. Bird migration can support seed dispersal at longer distances. However, we lack spatially explicit estimations of seed dispersal by migratory birds towards future climatically suitable ranges of plants. Thereby, it remains unclear to what extent they can facilitate plant redistribution in the coming decades. We integrated spatially explicit, seed‐dispersal models with projections on plant climatic suitability using species distribution models. We simulated long‐distance dispersal of 14 fleshy‐fruited plant species across Europe during the northward spring migration of song thrushes (Turdus philomelos), an adequate model species given its abundance, migratory behaviour and key role as disperser of native European plants. Dispersal models were replicated under three global warming projections and three scenarios of dispersal sensitivity to land‐cover alteration. Plant climatically suitable ranges will shift northwards by 248–948 km under severe warming projections by the year 2090. We identified a strong negative effect of warmer climate projections and higher dispersal sensitivity to land‐cover alteration on seed‐dispersal range filling (i.e. the proportion of future climatically suitable area that is currently unsuitable and receives seed‐dispersal events). Seed‐dispersal range filling averaged 22.2% across species under severe warming and assuming no sensitivity to land‐cover alteration. We found substantial interspecific variation in seed‐dispersal range filling, which was higher in species with lesser changes in their potential ranges and with smaller seeds dispersed over longer distances. Synthesis. Migrant frugivorous birds can partially assist fleshy‐fruited plants fruiting during spring migration to track climate change, although severe warming and land‐cover alteration may strongly constrain seed‐dispersal range filling. Importantly, range filling capacity is uneven across plant species: differences in climatically suitable ranges and intrinsic traits, particularly seed size, influence the ability of species to reach newly suitable areas. Interspecific variation in plant capacity to redistribute could be crucial for the reassembly of ecological communities under climate change. Resumen El cambio climático está provocando una redistribución global de la biodiversidad hacia áreas más frías a una velocidad sin precedentes. Las plantas son un componente clave de los ecosistemas terrestres y dependen principalmente de la dispersión de sus semillas para redistribuirse. Sin embargo, la mayoría de las semillas son dispersadas a distancias cortas (inferiores a un kilómetro), lo que resulta insuficiente para seguir el ritmo del cambio climático actual. La migración de las aves puede favorecer la dispersión de semillas a mayores distancias. No obstante, carecemos de estimaciones espacialmente explícitas de la dispersión de semillas por aves migratorias hacia las regiones que presentarán condiciones climáticas adecuadas en el futuro.…
n6c554239f11e: Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) is becoming increasingly popular but has not yet achieved its full potential due to the lack of cohesive workflows for processing large volumes of data. Although several tools support specific components of PAM analysis and some platforms integrate multiple functionalities, researchers often still rely on combinations of software and custom scripts to move from raw recordings to standardized and reproducible outputs. We present pamflow, an open‐source workflow for PAM built on Python and the robust Kedro framework, which provides a command‐line interface that enables execution of complete pipelines through standardized configuration files. It prioritizes broad usability through three key traits: open access, low computational requirements and streamlined workflow configuration. These features are intended to facilitate adoption in biodiverse but geographically isolated contexts, where limited budgets, constrained computational resources and scarce programming training are common. The tool is designed for users with varying levels of technical experience. While its use requires basic familiarity with command‐line tools and configuration files, its modular design also enables experienced programmers to extend, adapt, and customize workflows for research‐specific purposes. To illustrate our framework, we present the outputs obtained from a sampling conducted in Colombian Amazonia to support community forestry initiatives. The project was co‐led by the Humboldt Institute and the Foundation for Conservation and Sustainable Development (FCDS). The sampling was carried out through a participatory approach. Fourteen families and a local school participated in the installation of 38 recorders, capturing over 720 h of the local soundscape. Framed within open‐science principles, pamflow promotes data and technological sovereignty. In particular, we expect pamflow to (a) increase the adoption of PAM by providing an inclusive and open‐source solution that supports complete data processing workflows; (b) increase the number of biodiversity records reported from PAM projects to global biodiversity platforms such as GBIF; and (c) improve collaboration and data sharing among research groups and institutions by transforming input data into a globally accepted data standard. Resumen El Monitoreo Acústico Pasivo (PAM, por sus siglas en inglés) está adquiriendo una creciente popularidad, pero aún no ha alcanzado todo su potencial debido a la falta de flujos de trabajo integrados para procesar grandes volúmenes de datos. Aunque existen herramientas que apoyan componentes específicos del análisis acústico y algunas plataformas integran múltiples funcionalidades, los investigadores todavía suelen depender de combinaciones de programas y scripts personalizados para transformar grabaciones en bruto en resultados estandarizados y reproducibles. Presentamos pamflow, un flujo de trabajo de código abierto para monitoreo acústico pasivo desarrollado en Python y basado en Kedro. La herramienta proporciona una interfaz de línea de comandos que permite ejecutar procesos completos mediante archivos de configuración estandarizados. Su diseño prioriza la accesibilidad a través de tres características principales: licencia abierta, bajos requerimientos computacionales y una configuración simplificada del procesamiento de datos. Estas características buscan facilitar su adopción en lugares de alta biodiversidad pero geográficamente aislados, donde son comunes los presupuestos limitados, las restricciones en infraestructura computacional y las escasas oportunidades de formación en programación. La herramienta está diseñada para usuarios con distintos niveles de experiencia técnica aunque su uso requiera familiaridad básica con la línea de comandos y archivos de configuración.…
n28a40b274608: Demographic recovery is often used as evidence of conservation success, yet population growth does not necessarily restore maternally inherited genetic diversity. The Critically Endangered Chinese alligator (Alligator sinensis) has increased numerically under captive breeding, but contemporary maternal‐lineage representation remains poorly resolved. Here, we assembled control‐region‐excluded mitochondrial genomes from 356 individuals across six groups (F1, F2, F3, F4, wild and ZJ). Mitochondrial nucleotide diversity was extremely low (π = 5.41 × 10−5). Although 16 haplotypes were detected, 88.2% of sampled individuals carried only two dominant haplotypes, revealing pronounced matrilineal lineage compression. These findings show that demographic recovery can coexist with restricted contemporary representation of maternal lineages, underscoring that census growth alone does not constitute matrilineal recovery. Monitoring maternal lineages alongside nuclear genomic variation and census size can therefore provide a more complete assessment of conservation recovery.
na1e0aeb60de9: Migratory animals are potentially important parasite dispersers. However, understanding the impact of host migration on parasite distributions is challenging because variation in parasite life histories can mediate dispersal potential. Furthermore, studies of parasite dispersal via host migration often compare parasites in different species of migrant and resident hosts, despite differences in host phylogeny, ecology, and exposure history, which can complicate ascertaining the impact of migration. The Tasmanian population of silvereye Zosterops lateralis lateralis) exhibits partial migration. Some members of the population overwinter on the Australian mainland, where they co‐occur with residents of another silvereye subspecies (Z. l. cornwalli). Utilising targeted PCR, metabarcoding and high‐throughput sequencing, we characterise a range of parasite genera from blood and faecal samples in Tasmanian resident, migrant and mainland resident birds. Greater parasite richness was documented in migrant individuals, possibly reflecting exposure to varied parasite faunas at stopovers or during overwintering. The increased richness was primarily driven by parasites with simple life cycles. Reduced sharing of parasites with complex life cycles amongst migratory and resident host populations may be explained by ecological constraints in establishing transmission, such as vector or secondary host availability. Our study exemplifies the utility of molecular methods for characterising multi‐parasite systems and makes use of a single host species to provide insights on patterns of parasite distributions that result from migratory movements. Knowing how parasite life histories constrain or promote dispersal via regular host migration will be essential for predicting future patterns of pathogen dispersal under climate change and shifting migratory regimes.
n8d3a7e7d957b: Biogeographical analysis of species of Ranunculus sect. Euromontani and related taxa. Summary High mountain systems provide manifold preconditions for allopatric and sympatric speciation. We hypothesize that allopatric speciation due to geographical isolation of mountain chains, and sympatric speciation via allopolyploidy played major roles for a radiation within Ranunculus sect. Euromontani within the European Alpine System (EAS). We used target enrichment of 1249 nuclear gene loci on 81 samples for phylogenomics, biogeographical analysis, species delimitation, SNPs for genetic structure and NeighborNet analysis, flow cytometry for ploidy determination, and morphometrics for selected species pairs. We also included type material. The core R. sect. Euromontani comprises 12 monophyletic species, most of them (sub)endemic to one mountain system. The section originated probably from a widespread lineage and diversified 1.39 million years ago. Founder‐event speciation was the most common mechanism; only one species (Ranunculus montanus) originated likely in situ via allopolyploidy. In the West Carpathians, the new species Ranunculus tatrimontanus was recognized as different from Ranunculus gruinalis (= Ranunculus pseudomontanus) in the South Carpathians. In the Pyrenees, clinal variation suggested inclusion of Ranunculus ruscinonensis into Ranunculus gouanii. Peripatric speciation during the Pleistocene was the predominant mechanism for this geographical/climatic radiation in the EAS, whereas sympatric speciation via allopolyploidy happened only in the Alps.
n1fd9db67573c: Conceptual model of waterfowl‐mediated long‐distance dispersal in Ruppia sinensis. Summary Ruppia sinensis, a unique seagrass species that originated in the marine environment yet successfully colonized extreme inland habitats, offers a rare window onto how plants cope with major habitat shifts and clarifies the mechanisms of adaptive evolution during marine‐to‐brackish transitions. We assembled a chromosome‐level genome, conducted comparative phylogenomic analyses, assessed salinity tolerance through physiological experiments, and analyzed whole‐genome resequencing data from 103 individuals representing 19 coastal and inland populations. R. sinensis falls in the core seagrass PRC (Posidoniaceae, Ruppiaceae, and Cymodoceaceae) clade with a Ruppiaceae‐specific whole‐genome duplication yet has lost tolerance to full‐strength seawater and is an obligate brackish specialist. Coastal and inland lineages diverged c. 25 000 yr ago; dramatic sea‐level fluctuations since the Last Glacial Period repeatedly displaced coastal populations, causing reductions in effective population size, loss of genetic diversity, and elevated genetic load. Inland populations persisted in saline‐lake refugia and retain nearly twice the genetic diversity. The marine‐to‐brackish shift is an evolutionary trade‐off rather than passive habitat tracking, with inland saline lakes serving as refugia that preserved diversity. Such shifts may be a recurrent adaptive strategy in seagrass evolution, and these diverse inland populations warrant conservation priority under climate change.
n8201e2927aba: Safe havens are widely used to mitigate the impacts of invasive predators on threatened species, yet their isolation often disrupts evolutionary processes and can leave these species vulnerable to environmental change and stochastic events. Effective approaches to overcome these limitations and promote adaptive capacity in safe haven populations are lacking in conservation biology. Thus, we developed a pragmatic, heuristic management framework for integrating evolutionary principles into safe haven management with a focus on establishing a metapopulation of individuals distributed across geographically separated safe havens spanning environmental gradients. We used genetic simulations to demonstrate how this approach can enhance adaptive potential and persistence and to explore the optimal configuration of safe havens and number of individuals in each haven. Using demographic simulations for two threatened Australian mammals, we illustrated how this approach can be practically implemented. Based on spatially explicit population models, we predicted that many existing safe havens for these species are at risk of collapse within decades. However, our simulations showed that selection based on standing genetic variation can drive fitness gains within tens of generations, improving population resilience to novel conditions. Integrating these processes revealed that safe haven networks can promote adaptation and resilience, substantially improving long‐term persistence and providing robust sources for reintroductions. El desarrollo de la resiliencia evolutiva como marco para la gestión de las poblaciones en refugios seguros Resumen Los refugios seguros se utilizan ampliamente para mitigar el impacto de los depredadores invasores sobre las especies amenazadas; sin embargo, su aislamiento a menudo altera los procesos evolutivos y puede dejar a estas especies vulnerables a los cambios ambientales y a los eventos estocásticos. En la biología de la conservación se echan en falta enfoques eficaces para superar estas limitaciones y fomentar la capacidad de adaptación en las poblaciones de los refugios. Por ello, hemos desarrollado un marco de gestión pragmático y heurístico para integrar los principios evolutivos en la gestión de los refugios, centrándonos en el establecimiento de una metapoblación de individuos distribuidos entre refugios geográficamente separados que abarquen gradientes ambientales. Hemos utilizado simulaciones genéticas para demostrar cómo este enfoque puede mejorar el potencial de adaptación y la persistencia, así como para explorar la configuración óptima de los refugios y el número de individuos en cada uno de ellos. Mediante simulaciones demográficas de dos especies de mamíferos australianos amenazados, hemos ilustrado cómo se puede aplicar este enfoque en la práctica. Basándonos en modelos poblacionales espacialmente explícitos, predijimos que muchos de los refugios existentes para estas especies corren el riesgo de colapsar en unas décadas. Sin embargo, nuestras simulaciones mostraron que la selección basada en la variación genética existente puede impulsar mejoras en la aptitud en unas pocas decenas de generaciones, mejorando la resiliencia de la población ante condiciones nuevas. La integración de estos procesos reveló que las redes de refugios seguros pueden promover la adaptación y la resiliencia, mejorando sustancialmente la persistencia a largo plazo y proporcionando fuentes sólidas para las reintroducciones.
n97fe21f0c314: Understanding public sentiment toward wildlife is important for developing effective conservation practices and policies, and securing funding support. This holds true especially in the case of species such as the endangered dhole (Cuon alpinus), which carries a perception debt from centuries of negative attitudes. To examine whether historical negative perceptions are being amplified online, we applied a novel natural language processing (NLP) approach to >6,000 social media posts from Instagram, X (formerly Twitter), Facebook, and YouTube. We compared sentiment and engagement patterns associated with dholes against three other sympatric carnivores that vary in charisma and cultural visibility: Bengal tiger (Panthera tigris), sloth bear (Melursus ursinus), and golden jackal (Canis aureus). We quantified caption descriptors and sentiment across species and platforms, finding that dholes were disproportionately associated with negative adjectives and attitudes. Contrary to expectations, negative captions did not consistently accompany threatening or distressing visuals, highlighting a more complex relationship between language and media. Although audience engagement varied across thematic categories for some species, these differences were relatively small. Visual media outperformed text‐based content in eliciting online engagement. Together, these findings demonstrated how digital perceptions of wildlife are shaped by not only species identity but also content framing, platform dynamics, and media format. By integrating scalable NLP tools with targeted media analyses, we developed a replicable framework for decoding online sentiment and provided empirical insights that can inform conservation messaging strategies. Such approaches can be beneficial to researchers and organizations in rebalancing attention toward overlooked species and strengthening conservation narratives. Evaluación de la imagen que se ofrece en las redes sociales de especies problemáticas en peligro de extinción para diseñar mejores estrategias de comunicación en materia de conservación Resumen Comprender la opinión pública respecto a la fauna silvestre es importante para desarrollar prácticas y políticas de conservación eficaces y garantizar el apoyo financiero. Esto es especialmente cierto en el caso de especies como el perro silvestre asiático (Cuon alpinus), en peligro de extinción, que arrastra una «deuda de percepción» derivada de siglos de opiniones negativas. Para analizar si estas percepciones negativas históricas se están amplificando en Internet, aplicamos un novedoso enfoque de procesamiento del lenguaje natural (PLN) a más de 6.000 publicaciones en redes sociales procedentes de Instagram, X (antes Twitter), Facebook y YouTube. Comparamos los patrones de opinión y de interacción asociados a los perros silvestres asiáticos con los de otros tres carnívoros simpátricos que varían en cuanto a carisma y visibilidad cultural: el tigre de Bengala (Panthera tigris), el oso perezoso (Melursus ursinus) y el chacal dorado (Canis aureus). Cuantificamos los descriptores de los pies de foto y el sentimiento en todas las especies y plataformas, y descubrimos que los perros silvestres asiáticos se asociaban de forma desproporcionada con adjetivos y actitudes negativas. Contrariamente a lo esperado, los pies de foto negativos no acompañaban sistemáticamente a imágenes amenazantes o angustiosas, lo que pone de relieve una relación más compleja entre el lenguaje y los medios de comunicación. Aunque la interacción del público variaba según las categorías temáticas para algunas especies, estas diferencias eran relativamente pequeñas. Los medios visuales superaron al contenido basado en texto a la hora de generar interacción en línea.…
ndaccfe04a6c9: The commercial trade in exotic pets has raised concerns about population‐level impacts from collection in the wild; however, proponents of the trade claim that such concerns are unfounded. To resolve this debate, more information is needed on the volume of the pet trade, the species involved, their conservation status in the wild, and the relative numbers of wild‐caught versus captive‐bred animals. To examine these issues for reptiles and amphibians, we assembled and analyzed data on >255,000 specimens over a 16‐year period from the pricelists of a major commercial supplier in the United States and >85,000 specimens over a 6‐year period from suppliers in Europe. A small number of species dominated: 31% of listings included 22 species (14 snakes, four lizards, three frogs, and one turtle were all listed >2000 times). Of the 27 most commonly listed taxa, all were rated by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as least concern, except for two python species where collection for the pet trade is likely to be a minor threat compared with habitat destruction. The proportion of all listings that were described as captive‐bred rather than wild‐caught was approximately 34% and increased over time. There was no overlap between species that were in high demand for the pet trade versus for their meat and skins. We concluded that the major risks to reptiles and amphibians from the pet trade do not involve the unsustainable harvest of wild animals, but there are animal welfare issues and threats related to the spread of disease to wild populations and ecological and genetic impacts of released pets. Over the period that we surveyed, the numbers and types of reptiles and amphibians offered for sale by the U.S. and U.K. suppliers were unlikely to have imperiled populations of most species that were traded. Impacto mínimo del mercado comercial de mascotas exóticas sobre las poblaciones silvestres de reptiles y anfibios Resumen El mercado de mascotas exóticas ha suscitado preocupaciones sobre el impacto que tiene la captura en el medio natural sobre las poblaciones; sin embargo, los defensores de este comercio afirman que dichas preocupaciones carecen de fundamento. Se requiere de más información sobre el volumen del comercio de mascotas, las especies implicadas, su estado de conservación en su ambiente y las proporciones entre los animales capturados en estado silvestre y los criados en cautiverio para resolver este debate. Para realizar este análisis con reptiles y anfibios, recopilamos y analizamos datos sobre más de 255,000 ejemplares a lo largo de un periodo de 16 años, procedentes de las listas de precios de un importante proveedor comercial de Estados Unidos, y sobre más de 85,000 ejemplares a lo largo de un periodo de 6 años, procedentes de proveedores europeos. Un pequeño número de especies fue predominante: el 31% de las entradas correspondió a 22 especies (14 serpientes, 4 lagartos, 3 ranas y 1 tortuga, todas ellas mencionadas más de 2, 000 veces). De los 27 taxones que aparecieron con mayor frecuencia en las listas, todos estaban clasificados por la Unión Internacional para la Conservación de la Naturaleza (UICN) como de menor preocupación, salvo dos especies de pitón, en las que la captura para el comercio de mascotas probablemente suponga una amenaza menor en comparación con la destrucción de su hábitat. La proporción de todas las entradas descritas como criadas en cautiverio, en lugar de capturadas en estado silvestre, fue de aproximadamente el 34% y aumentó con el tiempo. No observamos que las especies con mayor demanda en el comercio de mascotas y aquellas con mayor demanda por su carne y sus pieles se traslaparan.…
n0e04781b177e: Habitat fragmentation is a major threat to freshwater biodiversity. In river networks, the dendritic structure of drainage systems can compound the effects of barriers to dispersal, which have greatly increased as a result of anthropogenic activities. Yet, disentangling the relative contributions of these natural and anthropogenic barriers remains challenging. We assessed how historical catchment isolation and contemporary river fragmentation jointly shape the genetic structure of a low‐dispersal freshwater fish, the Pyrenean minnow (Phoxinus bigerri), across northern Spain by genotyping 280 individuals from five independent catchments at 26 microsatellite loci and analysing genetic structure at regional and within‐catchment scales using STRUCTURE. The effects of fragmentation metrics on pairwise genetic differentiation were quantified with Maximum Likelihood Population Effects mixed models, and demographic histories were reconstructed using BOTTLENECK and DIYABC‐RF. Strong genetic differentiation among catchments was consistent with long‐term isolation, while pronounced substructure within several catchments suggested restricted contemporary connectivity. Among fragmentation metrics, the number of barriers between river reaches emerged as the strongest predictor of genetic differentiation, whereas cumulative barrier height and river distance showed weaker effects. Demographic analyses revealed signatures of recent bottlenecks, likely dating to the post‐medieval period and coinciding with intensified human modification of river networks. Together, these findings suggest that contemporary river fragmentation may reinforce genetic differentiation superimposed on older patterns of catchment isolation, highlight the pervasive impact of barriers on connectivity and provide insights relevant for the conservation and management of fragmented freshwater ecosystems.
n01b92f665095: Climate warming intensifies thermal selection on high-elevation species, yet the molecular mechanisms enabling rapid adaptation under ongoing gene flow remain poorly understood. We examined differentiation between High-elevation (High) and Low-elevation (Low) ecotype samples of Thitarodes xiaojinensis, an endemic ghost moth of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, using SLAF-seq, RNA-seq profiling and survival experiments. Phylogenetic analyses confirm the two ecotype samples are conspecific, and they differ in forewing phenotype. Population structure at K = 2 uncovers elevation-correlated clustering despite weak genome-wide structure (optimal K = 1). Genome-wide F ST scans (Weir & Cockerham) identify HSP60A as a prominent outlier locus (F ST = 0.391, top 1.4% of genome-wide windows). Targeted PCR amplification and sequencing confirmed a nonsense mutation (Glu378*) in the HSP60A coding sequence. This derived allele was carried by 80% (4/5) of Low individuals and by none of 5 High individuals (0 of 10 chromosome copies, one-sided 95% upper bound on allele frequency ≈ 26%), suggesting that it is associated with incipient ecological divergence between the two ecotypes. Co-expression network analysis grouped the chaperone genes into two systems with divergent thermal responses. The small HSPs were induced 2.3-fold from 8°C to 16°C, whereas the classical chaperones were not induced, and HSP60A was consistently placed within the latter (median biweight midcorrelation +0.56 with classical chaperones versus −0.27 with small HSPs, p = 3.5 × 10−9). Across the three temperatures the Low ecotype expressed HSP60A at lower levels than the High ecotype, significant under log2(TPM + 1) (p = 0.020) but not under the other two scales, and survived better at 16°C (p = 0.0342). These results link a coding variant at HSP60A, its lower transcript level in the Low ecotype and the better survival of that ecotype at 16°C, and identify HSP60A as a candidate locus for ecotype-informed conservation of the Ophiocordyceps sinensis host insect.
n34aaff7082a7: Whether invasive species conserve their ancestral climatic niches or undergo realized niche changes during global spread fundamentally affects the reliability of invasion risk projections. We integrated ensemble species distribution models (SDMs), the extended COUE framework, and Multivariate Environmental Similarity Surfaces (MESS) to quantify the global climatic niche dynamics and invasion risk of Solanum rostratum Dunal (Solanaceae) across its native North America and four invaded regions. Macroecological modeling revealed a temperature‐driven, precipitation‐constrained distribution, where thermal availability and mean diurnal range dictated suitability, while precipitation extremes imposed strict limits. Cross‐regional analyses comparing true occurrence records revealed a highly heterogeneous continuum of realized niche dynamics. Populations in Australia and Russia–Eastern Europe exhibited strict climatic conservatism, occupying analogous climates with complete niche stability (S = 1.000). Western European populations displayed substantial niche unfilling (U = 0.321); however, 80.4% of this constituted abandonment (native climates absent from Europe), suggesting genuine dispersal limitation. In contrast, Chinese populations exhibited extensive colonization of novel climatic conditions. Although showing near‐complete stability strictly within available analogous climates (S = 0.998), 48.5% of the expansion‐related niche quantity in China occurred in non‐analog environments (pioneering), leading to poor projection transferability of the native SDM (Continuous Boyce Index = 0.166). These findings demonstrate that S. rostratum maintains ancestral climatic preferences where suitable environments are available while possessing the capacity to pioneer novel climatic spaces during global invasion. Integrating these expanded realized tolerances into a global ensemble SDM provides a robust, region‐specific risk assessment framework that improves projection accuracy and supports adaptive management under global environmental change.
n89a65d519527: Tolerance to humans in wild animals can lead to several conflict situations and contribute to a generally negative perception of these animals among people. When a wild animal becomes reliant on human‐derived food, dangerous situations can arise, posing risks to both animals and humans. The brown bear (Ursus arctos) is a controversial species in Romania, as it is protected but also responsible for incidents with livestock, crops, or even humans. In our study, we aimed to identify the factors that facilitate bear visits to the town of Băile Tușnad and assess their effects on bear behaviours associated with increased tolerance of humans. Using city surveillance cameras, we analysed bear behaviour in relation to the use of electric fences and the presence of garbage scattered around the bins, seeking for a better understanding of which factors should be mitigated or adjusted to improve the safety of both bears and citizens. Our results supported our hypotheses that frequent bear visits to garbage container islands are linked to the availability of garbage and insufficient protective measures, such as non‐activated electric fences. As the frequency of bear visits increased, we observed a decrease in fearful behaviours, such as hesitation before entering the container islands or scanning their surroundings while foraging. This suggests that the bears of Băile Tușnad, in addition to showing signs of food conditioning, were also exhibiting increased tolerance to the urban environment, both of which could serve as precursors of a more persistent tolerance to human activity in the long term.
n209ecc3004ed: Employing a meta-regression analytical approach, we aimed to identify patterns of morphological change based on the impacts of anthropizing habitat pressures and the competition between native and invasive congeners. We harvested data from records for two species of Anolis lizards: Green Anoles (Anolis carolinensis), native to the southeastern USA, and invasive Cuban Brown Anoles (Anolis sagrei). We compared forest and urban habitats and for A. sagrei, native and invasive ranges. Our model analyzed variation in patterns of morphological size from 126 sex-specific samples measured in snout–vent lengths (SVL). We used two temporal scales: collection intervals (grouped in 5-year bins) and the estimated length since regional establishment of invasive A. sagrei (measured in decades). In post-hoc weighted regression analyses we evaluated the impact of island size on native and invasive populations. We found males were consistently larger than females and invasives were larger than natives. Island native anoles’ size correlated negatively with island area while invasive populations showed no correlation. Temporal predictors counteracted each other. We interpret these contradictions to show patterns of publication bias (5-year interval) and time since invasive establishment showing pressure driven morphological change. In forested habitats, invasives A. sagrei increase in size the longer the congeners coexist while A. carolinensis appear to shrink. In urban habitats, both congeners decrease in size the longer they coexist.
nf7bf197303e8: Nature is understood as a part of human life through sacred narratives to sustain the environmental resources. When nature is exposed to environmental disturbances such as climate change, it adapts to these imbalances and restructures itself to maintain a stable state. This article employs the idea of ‘isomorphism’ to investigate self-regulation and transformation of marine ecology through mythological narratives. By drawing on Eugene Odum’s idea of ‘Homeostasis’ and Sterling and Eyer’s ‘Allostasis’, the self-regulation and transformation process of the marine system is explored in the paper. The marine ecosystem undergoes internal self-regulations naturally to sustain equilibrium despite minor fluctuations reflecting ‘homeostasis’. However, when environmental disturbances such as coral bleaching, rise in ocean temperature, etc., exceeds the ecological resilience, the ecosystem reorganizes the structure itself and continues to function without collapsing, reflecting the ‘allostatic’ state. ‘Homeostatic’ and ‘Allostatic’ self-regulatory functions find narrative parallels in Greek and Hindu mythological traditions. Mythological marine narratives often portray the disrupt symbolic orders, reorganise divine authority and restructure the system, reflecting restoration and transformation of the systematic order. The mythological marine narratives and the marine ecosystem restoration exhibit binary oppositions, presenting conflicting forces within a single ecological system. The article employs Levi-Stauss’ theory of binary oppositions to argue that both ecological and mythological systems are bridged through opposing elements such as purification and pollution, creation and destruction, etc. This research explores marine space as a common entity where equilibrium is repeatedly disturbed, destabilised and restructured. The restoration of marine equilibrium has been adopted as one of the key objectives by the United Nations under Sustainable Development Goals. The paper also focuses on Sustainable Development Goal 14 – ‘Life Below Water’, by highlighting the conservation and sustainment of marine resources.
nafc2b07be2f5: BackgroundTropical coastal seascapes rely on ecological connectivity between mangrove, seagrass, and coral reef habitats to sustain fish biodiversity and fisheries productivity. However, identifying key fish species that facilitate cross-habitat energy flows remains challenging due to limitations of traditional survey methods in turbid, structurally complex environments.MethodsWe integrated environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding with Random Forest (RF) machine learning to map fish assemblages across a mangrove-seagrass-coral reef continuum in Hainan Island, South China Sea.ResultsWe detected 234 fish species across 78 families - a 4.03-fold increase over conventional gillnet surveys (58 species, paired t-test, t = 11.34, p < 0.001). Using RF classification, we identified 23 "connector species" with high cross-habitat fidelity, of which three super-connectors - Lutjanus russellii, Siganus fuscescens, and Gerres oyena - accounted for 47% of cross-habitat network flow. Simulated removal of these three species reduced overall network connectivity by 68%. The RF model achieved 90.7% accuracy (Kappa = 0.86) in predicting habitat occurrence from eDNA data. Variable importance analysis revealed a salinity threshold at 28 PSU and a distance-to-reef threshold at 2.5 km as primary drivers of community turnover. Our bipartite network analysis showed significant nestedness (NODF = 47.3, p < 0.001), indicating that generalist species disproportionately maintain seascape connectivity.DiscussionThese findings demonstrate that integrating eDNA with machine learning provides a scalable, high-resolution toolkit for defining functional connectivity and prioritizing species for ecosystem-based fisheries management in the Anthropocene.
n639735d2a59f: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract The functional composition of communities reflects species performance and its interplay with local and regional drivers. Yet trait‐based analyses often overlook regional heterogeneity (geographic and environmental differences among communities), despite its central role for community assembly. This limits our ability to assess functional change across broad spatial extents or long time periods, which is essential to understand the functional consequences of global change. To overcome this limitation, here, we expand the network analysis of traits (NATs) to assess community functional structure along spatial and environmental gradients by shifting the focus from species–trait associations to trait–trait co‐occurrences. We sequentially aggregated communities by (1) spatial proximity, (2) environmental similarity or (3) random selection to quantify how spatial and environmental gradients determined the density of links between trait co‐occurrences (i.e. trait associations) within networks (measured as edge density) and the position of individual traits within those networks (measured as trait strength and betweenness). We developed this approach using long‐term datasets of aquatic benthic invertebrate communities from Sweden: 56 lakes (spanning 21 years) and 39 streams (spanning 12 years) and compared their patterns with those obtained using in silico metacommunities. We found clear scale dependence on functional structure and contrasting regional drivers across ecosystems. While streams were only structured by geographic distance, the influence of environmental filtering increased over time in lakes, potentially signalling the effects of climate change on their functional structure. These results demonstrate that the relative importance of spatial and environmental drivers of functional structure can differ among freshwater ecosystems and change over time, highlighting the need to consider both regional heterogeneity and temporal dynamics when assessing functional metacommunity structure. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Resum La composició funcional de les comunitats reflecteix el rendiment de les espècies i la seva interacció amb els factors determinants locals i regionals. No obstant això, les anàlisis basades en trets sovint passen per alt l'heterogeneïtat regional (diferències geogràfiques i ambientals entre comunitats), tot i el seu paper central en l'assemblatge de les comunitats. Això limita la nostra capacitat per avaluar el canvi funcional al llarg d'àmplies extensions espacials o de llargs períodes temporals, la qual cosa és essencial per entendre les conseqüències funcionals del canvi global. Per superar aquesta limitació, ampliem l'Anàlisi de Xarxes de Trets (Network Analysis of Traits, NATs) per avaluar l'estructura funcional de les comunitats al llarg de gradients espacials i ambientals, canviant el focus de les associacions espècie–tret cap a les concurrències tret–tret. De manera seqüencial, es van agregar les comunitats per (1) proximitat espacial, (2) similitud ambiental, o (3) selecció aleatòria per tal de quantificar com els gradients espacials i ambientals determinen la densitat d'enllaços entre les concurrències de trets (és a dir, associacions de trets) dins de les xarxes (mesurada com a densitat d'enllaços) i la posició dels trets individuals dins d'aquestes xarxes (mesurada com la força i la centralitat d'intermediació del tret). Vam desenvolupar aquest enfocament utilitzant conjunts de dades a llarg termini de comunitats d'invertebrats bentònics aquàtics de Suècia: 56 llacs (al llard d'un període de 21 anys) i 39 rius (al llarg d'un període de 12 anys) i vam comparar els seus patrons amb els obtinguts mitjançant metacomunitats in silico.…
ncafde8c2bf40: Protected areas (PAs) are central to biodiversity conservation, yet their capacity to buffer species from climate‐driven heat exposure, that is, the duration and frequency of exposure to temperatures exceeding species' critical thermal limits, remains poorly quantified at global scales. Here, we assessed whether squamate reptiles inside PAs experience lower heat exposure than conspecifics in unprotected, human‐modified landscapes, and how this buffering effect varies across latitudes, biomes, and evolutionary lineages. Using biophysical modelling of operative temperatures across 248 species, we show that PAs consistently reduced both annual hours above critical thermal maximum (CTmax) and the frequency of critical days under current and future climatic scenarios (+2°C and + 4°C). We found that under current climate, protected sites had 51 fewer hours above CTmax and 3.5 fewer critical days than unprotected sites, and the proportional reduction persisted under +2°C and + 4°C warming scenarios. The buffering effect was most pronounced at low latitudes and tropical biomes, where species already operate close to their thermal limits. Deserts and xeric shrublands, together with tropical grasslands and savannas, emerged as biomes with elevated heat exposure, reinforcing growing concern for arid‐zone reptiles under climate change. Substantial phylogenetic signal in heat exposure indicated that evolutionary history shapes thermal vulnerability beyond geography and biome alone, with the magnitude of PA buffering varying considerably across squamate lineages. Our findings demonstrate that PAs can provide refugia from heat exposure, and that their conservation value under climate change depends on the retention of structurally complex habitats and thermally heterogeneous microhabitats.
n5d3341947c6e: The restoration of degraded ecosystems is critical for mitigating climate change and reversing biodiversity loss. Depending on the primary objective—such as maximizing carbon sequestration or protecting threatened species—and within the boundaries of budget limitations, different spatial priorities have been identified at global and regional scales. Funding mechanisms to support such work comprise public sources, philanthropy, and the private sector, including the sale of carbon and biodiversity credits. However, effectively exploring trade‐offs among restoration objectives and estimating the price of biodiversity and carbon credits to design financially viable projects remains scientifically challenging. Here we harness the power of artificial intelligence implemented in the software CAPTAIN to identify spatial priorities for ecological restoration that maximize multiple objectives at once and to allow a robust evaluation of biodiversity and climate outcomes. We find through a series of simulations that even low‐to‐moderate consideration of biodiversity in the design of restoration projects leads to the selection of restored areas that disproportionately improve the conservation of threatened species, while the carbon captured is only slightly reduced. We propose the bundling of biodiversity and carbon credits to support restoration efforts even in areas previously excluded for economic reasons. Applying our methodology to plant diversity in the Atlantic Forest of eastern South America, one of the most biodiverse and threatened ecosystems globally, we demonstrate its potential to guide restoration and to quantify trade‐offs between multiple optimization scenarios. Our study provides a robust, scalable method to maximize the joint benefits of ecological restoration for climate and nature. RESUMO A restauração de ecossistemas degradados é fundamental para mitigar as mudanças climáticas e reverter a perda de biodiversidade. Dependendo do objetivo principal—como maximizar o sequestro de carbono ou proteger espécies ameaçadas—e dentro dos limites impostos por restrições orçamentárias, diferentes prioridades espaciais têm sido identificadas em escalas globais e regionais. Os mecanismos de financiamento para apoiar esse tipo de trabalho incluem fontes públicas, filantropia e o setor privado, incluindo a venda de créditos de carbono e de biodiversidade. No entanto, um grande desafio científico é como explorar de forma eficaz as perdas e ganhos entre objetivos alternativos de restauração, e como estimar o preço de créditos de biodiversidade e de carbono para o planejamento de projetos financeiramente viáveis. Neste artigo, utilizamos o poder da inteligência artificial implementada no programa CAPTAIN para identificar prioridades espaciais para a restauração ecológica que maximizem múltiplos objetivos simultaneamente, e para permitir uma avaliação robusta dos resultados para a biodiversidade e o clima. Por meio de uma série de simulações, constatamos que mesmo uma consideração baixa a moderada da biodiversidade no planejamento de projetos de restauração leva à seleção de áreas restauradas que aumentam de forma desproporcional a conservação de espécies ameaçadas, enquanto o carbono capturado é reduzido apenas ligeiramente. Propomos a combinação de créditos de biodiversidade e de carbono para apoiar esforços de restauração mesmo em áreas anteriormente excluídas por razões financeiras. Ao aplicar nossa metodologia à diversidade de plantas da Mata Atlântica—um dos ecossistemas mais biodiversos e ameaçados do planeta—demonstramos o potencial da nossa ferramenta para planejar a restauração sob múltiplos cenários de otimização. Nosso estudo fornece um método robusto e escalável para maximizar os benefícios conjuntos da restauração ecológica para o clima e a biodiversidade.
n8231303c9fff: Animals increasingly move through landscapes very different from those in which their ecological strategies evolved, posing new challenges for ecologically specialized species. By tracking a forest‐dependent carnivorous bat across contrasting landscapes, this study shows how local habitat composition shapes landscape use, while behavioural flexibility remains bounded by species‐specific ecological requirements. Abstract Behavioural flexibility may allow animals to use heterogeneous landscapes, but the extent of this flexibility remains bounded by species‐specific habitat requirements. We examined how local landscape composition relates to habitat selection and foraging behaviour in Chrotopterus auritus, a forest‐dependent Neotropical carnivorous bat. We tracked 17 individuals across 57 nightly trajectories in 3 landscapes differing in local habitat composition and combined resource selection functions with hidden Markov models to evaluate habitat selection and the spatial expression of two inferred foraging strategies, active search and sit‐and‐wait. Evergreen and subdeciduous forests were consistently selected across trajectories and landscapes, whereas other forest types and most non‐forest land‐cover classes were not consistently selected. Associations with non‐forest elements were nevertheless highly variable among local contexts. Agricultural areas, roads and other open elements were incorporated into some trajectories in the more heterogeneous landscapes, whereas movements in the most continuously forested landscape remained largely within forest. Despite this context‐dependent variation in landscape use, both inferred foraging strategies were expressed predominantly within evergreen and subdeciduous forest. Across individuals, these two forest types together accounted for more than 75% of the locations assigned to each strategy, whereas median percentages within individual non‐forest classes were generally below 5%. Land‐cover composition was more clearly associated with where the two strategies were expressed than with when individuals switched between them. Our findings show that behavioural flexibility can generate context‐dependent landscape use without removing the ecological requirements that constrain it. More broadly, the use of modified landscape elements should not be interpreted as reduced habitat dependence without identifying which components of habitat use vary across landscapes and which remain consistent.
n93bf03b69585: This Research Highlight explains why African forest elephants reduce bird species richness about as much as human disturbance does, but not for the same reason. New data from Mount Cameroon show elephant grazing reshapes bird communities while better preserving functional redundancy than human‐driven forest fragmentation, challenging how megaherbivore impacts are assessed. Abstract Research Highlight: Korejs, K., Hořák, D., Krystof, C., Sedlacek, O., Motombi, F., Ewome, F., Molua, L., Tache, J., Kamga, S., Christopher, J. & Riegert, J. (2026). Megafaunal engineering in the tropical rainforest: African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) reduce avian species richness but elevate functional diversity. Journal of Animal Ecology, https://doi.org/10.1111/1365‐2656.70369. Elephants are major ecosystem engineers, but their effects on animal communities may be more complex than expected. A 4‐year study on Mount Cameroon found that grazing by African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) reduced avian species richness to levels comparable with those in forest degraded by human activity. Yet, unlike human‐driven degradation, elephant grazing did not promote the replacement of forest‐specialist birds by open‐habitat generalists. Instead, it shifted communities towards understorey and terrestrial invertivores at the cost of large frugivores. Despite lower species richness, elephant‐grazed forests showed higher functional diversity but lower functional redundancy than undisturbed forest, suggesting a change in community composition rather than simple ecological impoverishment. These findings show that the ecological signature of megaherbivore‐driven disturbance differs fundamentally from anthropogenic disturbance, and that species richness alone may not adequately capture the ecological role and conservation value of large herbivores.
nf2816b483d82: Marine mammal monitoring provides critical data to inform species management and sustainable industrial development. Passive acoustic monitoring, in particular, can provide continuous, long‐term and non‐observer‐biased data, with a subset of systems capable of delivering data in near‐real time. Acoustic monitoring is increasingly required around industrial activities to assess impacts on marine mammals. However, while effective, these systems can be costly and pose human safety risks during at sea field operations, hindering adaptive management efforts. Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) is an emerging technology that converts underwater fibre optic cables into dense listening arrays providing data with high spatio‐temporal resolution. It is usually implemented from a dry end (e.g. from shore, from a substation or a platform) enabling real‐time data processing and communications. DAS implemented on the extensive existing infrastructure of telecommunication and energy industries, can detect and localize low‐frequency baleen whale vocalizations, including blue (Balaenoptera musculus) and fin whales (B. Physalus). Ongoing research seeks to extend its capabilities to broader taxonomic groups, including through custom fibre installations. DAS is a promising economic alternative or supplemental method for marine mammal monitoring. DAS is increasingly used by offshore industries for infrastructure monitoring, presenting dual‐use opportunities for simultaneous infrastructure and environmental assessment. Given the growing recognition of submarine cables as critical infrastructure, DAS implementations are likely to accelerate. The broad adoption of dual‐use DAS that allows for marine mammal monitoring requires dialogue between marine researchers, technology developers, ocean industries and policymakers. Operational DAS‐based marine mammal monitoring requires systematic advances in two critical areas to reach their full potential: (1) characterizing DAS performance across species‐relevant frequency ranges and cable configurations and (2) developing robust automated methods to process the massive spatial–temporal datasets generated. This review provides a development framework addressing these priorities through standardized protocols and algorithm benchmarking. Our recommendations emphasize open science collaboration to enable real‐time processing and adaptive management applications.
n0984d0e6eb5d: Biological network analysis has become an important approach for investigating interactions among microorganisms, genes, proteins, and environmental variables across ecology, microbiology, and molecular biology. In practice, however, turning an inferred network into a clear figure and a full set of downstream topology and module analyses remains laborious, because the required steps are spread across several packages and are often finished by hand in a graphics editor. In response to these challenges, we have developed ggNetView, an R package that provides a complete analytical workflow. Its upstream step constructs networks from a variety of data sources, and its downstream steps encompass topology analysis, module analysis, and network visualization. The package utilizes a unified graph object, offers functions for geometric layout construction and annotation, and enables different types of networks to share a consistent set of aesthetic mappings. Beyond visualization, ggNetView enables comparison of similar modules across multiple networks and supports association analysis of the entire network and its subnetworks with environmental variables to help identify candidate modules associated with environmental variables. ggNetView has been applied to microbiome co‐occurrence, WGCNA‐derived co‐expression, and protein–protein interaction networks. Across repeated runs with the same graph object and parameters, node coordinates are reproduced. The package is freely available at https://github.com/Jiawang1209/ggNetView. 摘要 生物网络分析已成为解析微生物、基因、蛋白质与环境变量之间相互作用的重要途径，在生态学、微生物学和分子生物学中广泛应用。但在实际操作中，从网络推断到一张清晰的网络图，再到完整的拓扑属性与模块分析，仍然十分繁琐，所需步骤分散在多个软件包中，不少环节还需要在图形编辑器里手工完成。 为此，我们开发了ggNetView。该R包提供了一套完整的工作流程:上游分析基于多种据源进行网络构建，下游分析覆盖拓扑分析、模块分析和网络可视化。该软件包采用统一的图对象，提供多种几何布局构建函数与注释功能，并支持不同类型的网络共享同一套美学映射。 除可视化外，ggNetView还能在多个网络之间比较相似的模块，并可对整个网络及其子网络与环境变量做关联分析，从而筛选出与环境因子相关的候选模块。 我们已将ggNetView应用于微生物组共现网络、WGCNA共表达网络和蛋白质相互作用网络。在相同图对象与参数下进行重复运行，节点坐标可完全复现。软件包可从https://github.com/Jiawang1209/ggNetView免费获取。
n83c7eebe41b7: Island archipelagos are ideal natural laboratories for studying genetic variation in populations of organisms. However, relatively little attention has been given to parasites associated with hosts from oceanic islands. Here, we focus on Common Ground Doves (Columbina passerina) and two ecomorphs of parasitic lice, Physconelloides eurysema body lice and Columbicola passerinae wing lice. Both louse species parasitize C. passerina doves and their close relatives but differ in their dispersal abilities. The doves and lice are widespread across the Caribbean archipelago and adjacent continents. We were interested in two primary questions: (1) do doves and lice have congruent phylogeographic histories? and (2) do island populations of doves and lice have reduced genetic diversity compared to mainland populations? To address these questions, we used genomic data from doves and lice to reconstruct phylogenetic relationships, assess population genetic structure, and estimate measures of genetic diversity. We found that genetic structure was not consistently congruent among the doves and lice, suggesting movement of the doves that is not apparent from their genetic information. Doves and lice also have different phylogeographic histories. Doves likely originated in the Caribbean islands, whereas lice originated in the mainland or dispersed multiple times between the mainland and islands. We also did not find strong evidence that island populations of doves or lice have less genetic diversity compared to mainland populations. Our results highlight that hosts are the most immediate ‘island’ for their parasites, but varying dispersal abilities and island geography can lead to discordant phylogeographic patterns over time.
n1b94e5ed6f5b: Mitonuclear incompatibilities are genetic mismatches between mitochondrial and nuclear genomes that initially arise through hybridization. Although these incompatibilities can reduce hybrid fitness and contribute to reproductive isolation, they remain poorly understood in most avian hybrid zones. To investigate mitonuclear discordance in the extensively studied hybrid zone between Bullock's (Icterus bullockii) and Baltimore Orioles (I. galbula), we used whole‐genome resequencing and mitochondrial haplotyping to assign mitochondrial ancestry to 136 individuals previously characterized for their levels of nuclear genomic admixture. We detected a narrow mitochondrial cline across the hybrid zone and strong asymmetry in mitochondrial inheritance, with 83% of putative F1 hybrids having I. galbula mitochondrial ancestry, a pattern consistent with predictions from Darwin's corollary to Haldane's rule involving uniparentally inherited loci. Genome‐wide association analyses revealed nonrandom associations between mitochondrial haplotype and autosomal nuclear loci, notably including candidate genes with mitochondrial functions. Population‐specific signals of positive selection at these loci further suggest differential selective pressures linked to mitochondrial ancestry. Together, our results provide evidence that mitonuclear interactions may contribute to asymmetric introgression and the maintenance of species boundaries in this classic avian hybrid zone.
n9dfe98d2b173: Proposed model of intracellular responses of Arabidopsis leaf mesophyll cells to photoinhibition, as suggested in this study. Summary Chlorophagy removes photodamaged chloroplasts in plants, while individual chloroplasts are also protected by mechanisms that limit damage to the photosynthetic apparatus caused by excess light energy, known as photoinhibition. How chlorophagy is functionally coupled with chloroplast‐level protective mechanisms during acclimation to photoinhibition remains unclear. We investigated acclimatory responses to photoinhibition at the intracellular level in Arabidopsis thaliana through an integrative analysis combining Chl fluorescence measurements, microscopy imaging, and genetic analyses using mutants defective in nonphotochemical quenching (NPQ) or the chloroplast avoidance response. The functionality of individual chloroplasts was further assessed by Chl fluorescence lifetime imaging and probe‐based visualization of singlet oxygen and starch. Severe photoinhibition of photosystem II precedes the appearance of abnormally swollen chloroplasts, which are subsequently recognized by the autophagy machinery for degradation. The swollen chloroplasts represent irreversibly damaged chloroplasts that accumulate reactive oxygen species and lose photosynthetic function. The formation of these nonfunctional chloroplasts was enhanced in mutants defective in NPQ or the chloroplast avoidance response, and hyperaccumulation of nonfunctional chloroplasts led to necrotic cell death. Together, our findings illustrate how multilayered responses coordinate acclimation to photoinhibition: Chloroplast protective mechanisms minimize the formation of nonfunctional chloroplasts while chlorophagy removes them when they arise.
n893e480914c0: Model for strigolactone regulation of basal iron uptake in Arabidopsis and maize. Summary Strigolactone (SL) hormones influence a wide range of developmental and physiological processes but have not previously been linked to plant iron homeostasis. Here, we identify the gene underlying the iron‐deficient maize mutant interveinal yellow (ivy) as ZmCCD8, a key enzyme in SL biosynthesis. Maize ivy/ccd8 mutants exhibit reduced expression of iron‐regulated genes, including IRO2 and genes involved in iron chelator and transporter biosynthesis. Application of the synthetic SL rac‐GR24 restores gene expression and alleviates chlorosis. Under iron‐deficient conditions, ccd8 mutants show normal upregulation of iron uptake genes, indicating that SLs are not required for the deficiency response but are essential for maintaining basal iron gene expression under sufficient iron. Similar chlorosis in Arabidopsis and rice SL mutants under moderate iron suggests a conserved role for SLs in iron regulation, with potential agricultural applications. We propose that strigolactone signaling acts as an upstream regulatory input to the established FIT/IRO2‐centered iron‐deficiency network, with SMXL/D53 proteins functioning as negative regulators and iron deficiency providing the principal activating cue.
nff6de229dad7: The cyanobacterium Anabaena exhibits remarkable morphological plasticity in response to changes in light intensity. These reversible changes are associated with the repositioning of thylakoids within the cytoplasm. Here, we show that cell morphology is determined by the balance between the activities of two peptidoglycan assembly systems, the elongasome and class A penicillin‐binding proteins, which respond oppositely to light intensity. By modulating light absorption and photosynthetic performance, changes in cell morphology enable large globular cells to mitigate the deleterious effects of high‐light stress, revealing morphological plasticity as a previously unrecognized mechanism of acclimation to high light. Summary Phytoplankton species display characteristic morphologies that are generally assumed to confer adaptive advantages, yet the functional significance of cell shape remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether pleomorphism contributes to acclimation to changing light environments. Using the cyanobacterium Anabaena sp. PCC 7120 as a model system, we combined molecular genetics, microscopy, physiological measurements and biophysical analyses to determine how morphology is regulated and how it affects photosynthetic performance under different light intensities. We show that Anabaena undergoes a reversible light‐dependent morphological transition from rod‐shaped cells under low light to large globular cells under high‐light stress. This transition is controlled by the relative activities of the elongasome and class A penicillin‐binding proteins and is accompanied by thylakoid reorganization. The globular morphology reduces light absorption and enables cells to maintain photosynthetic activity under photoinhibitory conditions. Our findings establish a mechanistic link between cell‐wall remodeling, cellular optics and photosynthetic performance, revealing pleomorphism as a dynamic acclimation strategy to high‐light stress. More broadly, this work provides experimental support for the packaging effect and highlights morphology as an active determinant of phytoplankton acclimation capacity.
nac83449e4eee: “Statistical significance”, wherein the deviation of some measure of a sample population is greater than an expected threshold (usually p > 0.05) is a concept and practice strongly embedded in the life sciences. However, the use of “statistical significance” has been deprecated by the American Statistical Association (ASA), and that news has been slow to spread across disciplines. The result of this misuse is that many authors are wrongfully claiming “no effect” of a variable when p > 0.05 or confidence intervals (CIs) overlap zero. To ensure scientific rigor in Ecology and Evolution, we offer this brief guide to authors and reviewers and strongly encourage authors to use the ASA statement on p‐values. The ASA suggests that authors report effect sizes and attendant error in ways that let users judge support for the hypotheses represented in a model, avoiding the binary “true or false” of p = 0.05 or overlapping CIs. Furthermore, we encourage authors to acquaint themselves with numerous other common mistakes in statistical interpretation highlighted by the ASA and subsequent authors. By incorporating these principles into statistical reporting and results, information and patterns that might otherwise be overlooked remain available for readers to evaluate. We recognize that changes in reporting practices will not occur overnight, so our aim is to help authors adopt ASA principles: to that end we describe potential problems and offer guidelines for authors and reviewers to follow, to avoid incorrect statistical interpretations and spurious conclusions.
n10d6ac70187c: Species distribution models often assume that species occupy all environmentally suitable space, but low-dispersal amphibians may track landscape structure that has persisted over long periods as well as current local conditions. We examined how broad-scale landscape structure and fine-scale microhabitat jointly shape the distribution of the Jeju salamander, Hynobius quelpaertensis, on Jeju Island, Republic of Korea. Using 85 spatially thinned occurrence records and 10,000 background points sampled on land, we compared a broad-scale predictor set (terrain at ≥ 1 km, drainage position and long-term climate, used as a proxy for a long-term topographic-hydrological template) with a fine-scale set (microtopography, wetness, insolation and canopy). Weighted elastic-net models were evaluated by spatial block cross-validation with block-bootstrap confidence intervals, and a generalized additive model (GAM) with broad-scale suitability as an offset tested whether microhabitat refined occupancy within broadly suitable space. The broad-scale and fine-scale models discriminated occurrences equally well (ROC AUC = 0.79 and 0.78), but the broad-scale model was better calibrated (Tjur's R 2 = 0.16 vs. 0.12), and the combined model performed best (ROC AUC = 0.81; Tjur's R 2 = 0.20). Both sets identified drainage position: occurrence increased with upstream drainage area and local wetness and was higher in hollows and valley bottoms. Within the broad-scale core, fine-scale smooth terms doubled Tjur's R 2 (0.14 to 0.28): occurrence rose with canopy shade and valley depth and declined on exposed south-facing slopes, although the gain in discrimination was uncertain. Areas suitable only at the fine scale covered 24% of the island but had one-sixth the presence rate of areas suitable at both scales. Valley drainage structure thus sets the template for the distribution of H. quelpaertensis, and shaded, moist microhabitat refines occupancy within it. Conservation should maintain drainage networks together with their forest cover, and candidate unoccupied areas should be surveyed in the field.
nb7c70620f780: Crop wild relatives represent important sources of genetic variation for crop improvement, particularly as climate change and increasing global food demand require the development of more resilient and productive crop varieties. However, genomic information on many wild Dioscorea species in East Asia remains limited. In this study, we sequenced and assembled the complete chloroplast genomes of six Dioscorea species native to Korea, including the first reported complete chloroplast genome of D. coreana. The assembled genomes exhibited a conserved quadripartite structure with similar gene contents and GC compositions across species. Despite this overall conservation, comparative analyses revealed localized sequence variation, particularly in noncoding regions. Several loci, including ndhF and ycf1, exhibited increased nucleotide diversity, indicating their potential as informative markers. In addition, simple sequence repeats were composed mainly of A/T‐rich motifs and predominantly distributed in the large single‐copy region. Phylogenetic analysis based on concatenated chloroplast protein‐coding gene sequences provided a well‐resolved framework for the studied taxa and clarified the relationships among Korean Dioscorea species. Furthermore, the close genetic relationship between cultivated yam and its wild relatives was supported. These results provide new genomic data for previously underrepresented Korean taxa, including the first chloroplast genome of D. coreana, and offer a basis for future studies on genetic diversity, species identification, and the utilization of wild germplasm.
n53361b2e8e60: Parasites are increasingly utilized as surrogates for investigating host ecology. Digenean trematodes (“flukes”) have been identified as promising bioindicators because they have obligate multi‐host life cycles that often include an abundant and accessible gastropod intermediate host and one or more vertebrate definitive hosts. Definitive vertebrate hosts are typically the mechanism for dispersal by flukes, thus driving congruent patterns in population genetic structure between host and parasite. This suggests that flukes can function as surrogates for understanding dispersal of their vertebrate hosts. Here, we investigated the terrapin fluke Pleurogonius malaclemys as a surrogate for its definitive diamondback terrapin host Malaclemys terrapin. This parasite is reliant on its intermediate host, the eastern mudsnail Ilyanassa obsoleta, as well as terrapin final hosts. We hypothesized that there would be high population genetic structure across fluke populations, reflecting the limited dispersal rates and low population connectivity of terrapin hosts. Specimens of Pleurogonius malaclemys were sampled from mudsnails (internal first‐intermediate and external cyst stages) and from terrapins (adult stage) across their co‐occurring range from Massachusetts to northeast Florida. Fluke mitochondrial DNA was extracted and sequenced, and a 620 bp fragment was used for population genetics analyses. Asexually reproducing larval fluke stages were rare within mudsnails (often 0%, but never exceeding 3.85%), while external cysts were common on mudsnails (up to 74%). About 45% of terrapins from southern New Jersey harbored adult flukes. Genetics analyses revealed high diversity and population genetic structure in flukes, broadly consistent with reported patterns for terrapins. Our study provides baseline genetic data and a foundational understanding of the biogeography and diversity of the terrapin fluke, thereby identifying a promising surrogate for terrapin population ecology and subsequent conservation efforts.
n263a8a316b6f: This study evaluates the relationship between MaxEnt-predicted habitat suitability and departmental estimates of population density for 14 game mammal species in the Pavlodar Region. Model performance varied substantially among species (Test AUC = 0.538–0.992; TSS = 0.220–0.984), and extremely high AUC values for some species with small samples were interpreted cautiously. For 41 territorial units, habitat suitability was aggregated as the mean MaxEnt value within each polygon and compared with density using Spearman's rank correlation. Spearman's r s ranged from 0.288 to 0.738; in the initial analysis, a statistically significant positive relationship was detected for 13 of the 14 species, whereas the relationship was not statistically significant for the steppe polecat (r s = 0.288; p = 0.068). Residual spatial autocorrelation assessed with Moran's I was non-significant for 11 species; for wolf, bobak marmot, and roe deer, an additional spatially constrained permutation analysis was performed. After this analysis, the relationship remained significant for wolf (r s = 0.714, p = 0.0007) and roe deer (r s = 0.488, p = 0.0198), whereas for bobak marmot it remained positive but was not statistically significant after accounting for spatial structure (r s = 0.467; p = 0.0615). The results indicate that habitat suitability reflects the environmental potential of an area but is not a direct measure of population density.
n575a0a7a03e2: Understanding how reproductive isolation is maintained between closely related taxa is a central question in evolutionary biology. Here, we investigate the mechanisms underlying divergence and isolation between two sister butterflies, Erebia palarica and Erebia meolans, which occur in sympatry in the Cantabrian Mountains (N Spain) and in allopatry elsewhere. Using an integrative approach, we combine genetic, genome synteny and cytogenetic analyses, Wolbachia screening, and geometric morphometrics to assess their evolutionary history and elucidate potential reproductive barriers between these species. The phylogeographic pattern suggests that both species diverged in allopatry, coming into secondary contact along the Cantabrian Mountains after the last glacial maximum. Both mitochondrial and nuclear markers recover reciprocal monophyly, indicating the absence of recent hybridisation. The identical chromosome numbers in both species (2n = 28), the absence of major chromosomal rearrangements or straightforward genitalia differentiation, and the presence of the same Wolbachia strain in all infected individuals suggest that neither chromosomal rearrangements nor Wolbachia‐induced incompatibilities contribute to their reproductive isolation in sympatry. In contrast, morphometric analyses show a significant divergence in wing size consistent with asymmetric character displacement: sympatric populations of E. palarica exhibit larger wings relative to both allopatric conspecifics and sympatric E. meolans, whereas E. meolans shows little size variation across northern Spain. Our findings point to wing size divergence in E. palarica as a response to sympatry with E. meolans. Overall, this study provides novel empirical evidence for morphometric character displacement in the family Nymphalidae, highlights the importance of multidisciplinary approaches for understanding species differentiation, and sets a framework for future genomic studies of speciation and reproductive isolation between closely related taxa.
n0f1ba30bfebd: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Dormancy allows animals to persist through prolonged periods of unfavourable environmental conditions by entering states of extreme metabolic depression. However, physiological responses to dormancy vary substantially across taxa and can involve changes in redox balance, immune function and endocrine adjustments. A key unresolved question is whether this variation reflects fundamental differences in how endotherms and ectotherms regulate metabolic depression and subsequent reactivation, with implications for understanding animal life histories and responses to climate change. Here, we conducted a meta‐analysis to test whether physiological responses to dormancy differ between endothermic and ectothermic animals. We synthesised 2464 effect sizes from 106 studies across 57 species, quantifying redox, immune and glucocorticoid status during dormant and arousal states relative to active, non‐dormant state, under cold‐ and heat‐induced dormancy. In endotherms, dormant and arousal states were associated with reduced oxidative damage and reactive oxygen species production, together with increased antioxidant and redox‐regulatory activity, indicating robust maintenance of redox homeostasis across metabolic transitions. In contrast, ectotherms experienced increased oxidative damage during the dormant state under both cold‐ and heat‐induced conditions, with little evidence for compensatory antioxidant responses. Immune function also diverged across thermoregulatory strategies: while endotherms showed no overall suppression of immune function during dormancy and an increase in innate immune responses during arousal, ectotherms tended to downregulate both innate and adaptive pathways during the dormant state. By contrast, glucocorticoid levels did not show consistent changes across dormancy states in either group. Our study shows that the physiological consequences of animal dormancy vary across thermoregulatory strategies. Endothermy seems to buffer the oxidative and immunological challenges associated with metabolic depression, whereas dormancy in ectotherms is associated with physiological trade‐offs that may limit adaptive capacity to changing conditions. Our synthesis highlights metabolic depression as a key axis linking thermoregulation to variation in physiology, with implications for the evolution of life histories and prediction of species responses to ongoing environmental change.
