n7473ba318101: Although climate‐driven changes in ocean circulation are increasingly recognized as key drivers of marine ecosystem structure and dynamics, their consequences for the early life stages of deep‐sea fishes remain difficult to quantify. In the Southern Ocean, variability in frontal systems such as the Polar Front (PF) may influence larval dispersal and retention, with direct implications for recruitment. We investigated how interannual variability in ocean circulation and egg production shapes larval dispersal and retention in suitable recruitment areas of a large body size deep‐sea fish species, Patagonian toothfish (Dissostichus eleginoides), around the Kerguelen Plateau. We developed an integrated modeling framework which combined spatially explicit models of egg production with 24 years (2000–2023) of Lagrangian dispersal simulations driven by satellite‐derived geostrophic currents to quantify successful larval retention. Ontogenetic changes in distribution and fecundity were accounted for to model egg production, allowing retention metrics to reflect spatial heterogeneity in reproductive output. Larval retention rate in suitable recruitment areas varied from 9% to 28% over the study period. PF‐associated jet intensity was significantly associated with larval retention variability: years characterized by stronger PF‐associated circulation showed lower larval retention, with more larvae advected away from the shelf toward the eastern part of the plateau. The latter part of the time series, particularly after 2010, was characterized by stronger year‐to‐year fluctuations, a higher contribution of the North‐West recruitment area, and more frequent low‐retention years. Building on new findings on toothfish spawning dynamics and long‐term altimetry data, we showed for the first time that there is the potential for self‐recruitment in the northern part of the Kerguelen Plateau (French EEZ). We also discussed the implications for fishery management since PF‐associated indices may help interpret past recruitment trends and offer useful early‐warning for future recruitment anomalies.
n34e78daf9ea0: Over millennia, social and ecological systems have been shaped by fire and have in turn shaped fire regimes. However, recent decades have seen an escalating “fire crisis” characterized by an increasing incidence of large, intense wildfires, most notably in forests. Voices in the academic literature and media often attribute the fire crisis to a narrow range of mechanisms, for example, fuel management or climate change. This failure to acknowledge the complexity of causes leads to simplistic framings of risk, and ultimately, proposed solutions that are either not feasible or may lead to undesired outcomes. In this review we outline the human and bioclimatic factors that are driving this fire crisis. Factors reviewed include the impacts of colonial legacies, which disrupted Indigenous land stewardship and traditional burning practices over centuries; policies of fire suppression; population growth, urbanization and land management practices; biotic disturbances such as insect outbreaks and invasive plant species; and climate change, which is affecting both fire regimes and social‐ecological resilience to fire. Many of these factors co‐occur leading to complex interactions and, often, unexpected outcomes. Our review highlights that climate change is now having a compounding effect, building on a multitude of other factors to drive the fire crisis. Addressing this crisis requires first acknowledging its complexity and moving beyond simple framings of risk. We suggest solutions will vary across different places and through time, but may include supporting Indigenous land stewardship, adopting flexible fire responses, shifting societal expectations from aggressive fire suppression to “living with fire”, and fostering resilient social and ecological communities.
n0d26cbd952a4: Increasing soil organic carbon (SOC), central to food security and climate mitigation, is increasingly recognized as being mediated by microbial necromass C (MNC) accrual. However, how microbial production and mineral preservation jointly govern MNC accrual under contrasting resource conditions remains unclear. Here, we analyzed soils from 14 long‐term fertilization experiments (up to 47 years) to assess how edaphic and climatic conditions regulate the response of MNC accrual to manure (M) and non‐manure (NM) fertilization treatments. We found that the primary constraints on MNC accrual varied with resource availability, with microbial production under resource‐limited conditions and mineral preservation under resource‐abundant conditions. Under resource‐limited conditions, M treatments increased MNC by up to 122%, with changes tightly coupled to SOC gains. This accrual was associated with increases in dissolved organic C and microbial C use efficiency, indicating a production‐constrained pathway in which manure inputs alleviate substrate limitation and promote microbial C allocation toward biomass production and necromass formation. Conversely, under resource‐abundant conditions, MNC responses to fertilization were weaker (+56%) and uncoupled from SOC gains. Instead, MNC accrual was primarily associated with mineral protection capacity (e.g., Fe and Al oxides), consistent with a preservation‐constrained pathway. Overall, microbial processing and mineral preservation represent context‐dependent constraints on MNC accrual under contrasting resource conditions. These findings underscore the importance of resource context for site‐specific C management and for understanding soil C dynamics under global change.
n92694bcbdcc6: Accelerating environmental change in the Antarctic and Southern Ocean (ASO) necessitates robust extinction risk assessments to inform conservation priorities. Nevertheless, no systematic, region‐wide baseline of extinction risk currently exists for tracking ASO biodiversity responses to ongoing change, a significant barrier to global biodiversity monitoring. Here, we conducted the first ASO‐wide synthesis of current extinction risk knowledge for plants, animals and Fungi. This included examining biases in current assessments, the distribution of Threatened species and their associated threats. Using a data‐inclusive workflow, we compiled 8908 assessments representing 4970 species, more than doubling the number of ASO species assessed compared with any single source. As expected, assessments were heavily biased towards vertebrates (58% assessed), while invertebrates, despite their ecological prevalence, were markedly underrepresented (6% assessed). Among vertebrates, mammals had the highest proportion of Threatened species (26%). Birds within the ASO were disproportionately Threatened (25%) compared to the global average (11%), with the greatest threat for ASO species being ‘Biological Resource Use’. The sub‐Antarctic Islands had the highest density of both Threatened species and assessment effort, whereas many Antarctic species remain unassessed. Additionally, Threatened species have the lowest protected area coverage of any conservation status. These pronounced assessment biases highlight the need for more balanced, representative and data‐inclusive extinction risk assessments to be able to effectively detect conservation status change. This work represents an important step in ensuring ASO representation in global biodiversity monitoring frameworks, strengthening the capacity of these frameworks to detect, attribute and respond to future biodiversity changes.
nc463fbe6b3dc: Anthropogenic warming and shifts in global precipitation regimes are increasing rainfall variability and the frequency of intense precipitation events, raising uncertainty about how conventional meteorological drought indices capture ecosystem water limitation. This uncertainty arises from two key issues: temporal aggregation, as most meteorological drought indices are based on monthly integrated summaries, and drought definition, because atmospheric water deficits do not necessarily translate into vegetation water stress. Here, we quantified ecosystem gross primary productivity (GPP) responses to drought using three approaches: (1) monthly meteorological drought identified from monthly standardized precipitation evaporation index (SPEI), (2) daily meteorological drought defined by daily SPEI, and (3) ecological drought defined using an indicator of actual vegetation water limitation. Comparing monthly and daily SPEI‐based drought isolated the effects of temporal aggregation, while comparing daily meteorological and ecological droughts quantified the influence of drought definition. Across 130 eddy‐covariance sites spanning multiple biomes and climate zones, we analyzed 6691 drought months identified using monthly SPEI. Daily SPEI data revealed that within months classified as meteorological drought, nearly 50% of days did not coincide with atmospheric water deficits owing to daily rainfall variability. As a result, monthly SPEI overestimated GPP responses (20.60% ± 5.28% increase) relative to daily SPEI (4.61% ± 1.21% increase). In contrast, daily meteorological drought metrics underestimated drought‐induced suppression of GPP by ~46% compared with ecological drought, demonstrating that atmospheric drought metrics do not fully reflect water stress experienced by vegetation. Our results show that both temporal resolution and drought definition can bias estimates of ecosystem drought responses, underscoring the need for finer‐scale temporal and ecologically relevant measures of vegetation water limitation to improve understanding of biosphere–climate interactions in an increasingly drought‐prone world.
nd13de01d327b: By integrating tracking data from multiple migratory waterfowl species with remote sensing data, we showed that birds using more stopover sites are better able to synchronize their schedules with vegetation green‐up at their breeding grounds. Our findings highlight the importance of stopover sites in enhancing birds' resilience to climate change. Abstract Climate change is altering the phenology of food resources, and migratory birds may respond by adjusting migration timing to track shifting food availability (i.e. their phenological sensitivity). The ability to adjust migration timing can vary among species according to traits such as ecological guild, body size and migration distance. Stopover sites are critical components of migration, allowing birds to refuel and acquire updated environmental information. However, empirical evidence on how stopover use enhances phenological sensitivity to shifting spring green‐up remains lacking. In this study, we investigated how stopover frequency influences the phenological sensitivity of migratory waterfowl at breeding areas. We hypothesized that individuals using more stopover sites would better align their migration timing with shifts in vegetation green‐up. We reconstructed 220 spring migration paths from five East Asian migratory waterfowl species using high‐resolution tracking data collected from 2015 to 2023. Spring vegetation green‐up was derived from remote sensing data. We then fitted linear mixed models to test how stopover frequency influences the change of arrival timing at breeding sites. Individuals using a greater number of stopover sites showed closer alignment between their migration timing and local spring vegetation green‐up at breeding areas. More frequent stopover use was associated with stronger phenological sensitivity, suggesting greater behavioural plasticity in tracking shifting resources. Loss of stopover habitat may therefore limit their capacity to respond to changing resource phenology, underscoring the importance of stopover conservation for promoting resilience to climate change. 中文摘要 气候变化正在改变食物资源的物候，迁徙鸟类可能通过调整迁徙时间来追踪不断变化的食物可利用性，即表现出对资源物候变化的物候敏感性。不同物种调整迁徙时间的能力可能因生态类群、体型和迁徙距离等性状而异。停歇地是迁徙过程中的关键组成部分，不仅为鸟类提供补充能量的场所，也有助于其获取最新的环境信息。然而，关于停歇地利用如何影响迁徙鸟类对春季植被返青变化的物候敏感性，目前仍缺乏实证证据。 本研究探讨了停歇地利用频率如何影响迁徙水鸟在繁殖地的物候敏感性。我们假设，利用更多停歇地的个体能够更好地调整迁徙时间，从而使到达繁殖地的时间与春季植被返青变化保持更紧密的同步。 基于2015‐2023年高分辨率追踪数据，我们重建了5种东亚迁徙水鸟共220条春季迁徙路线，并利用遥感数据获取春季植被返青时间。随后，我们构建线性混合效应模型，检验停歇地利用频率对繁殖地到达时间变化的影响。 结果表明，利用更多中途停歇地的个体，其迁徙时间与繁殖地当地春季植被返青变化之间表现出更高程度的匹配。中途停歇地利用数量越多，个体表现出的物候敏感性越强，表明更频繁地利用中途停歇地可能有助于迁徙水鸟通过行为可塑性追踪不断变化的资源物候。因此，中途停歇地栖息地的丧失可能限制迁徙水鸟应对资源物候变化的能力。这一发现凸显了保护迁徙停歇地对于增强其应对气候变化能力的重要性。
n9ee892f52045: Biogeographic barriers are fundamental in shaping the distribution of animals and plants, yet the role of discrete landscape features in constraining microbial dispersal remains poorly understood. Identifying the barriers that partition gut microbial communities is essential for modelling the distribution of hosts and their symbionts across physical space and evolutionary time. The deer mouse (Peromyscus maniculatus species complex), which inhabits nearly all terrestrial environments in North America, provides an ideal model for testing these biogeographic drivers of the mammalian gut microbiome. Using NSF NEON biorepository samples, we characterized the gut microbiomes of 13 populations across the contiguous United States using full‐length 16S rRNA long‐read sequencing. The presence or absence of microbial taxa was best explained by eastern versus western regions compared to habitat or climate, suggesting a role of large fluvial systems as discrete barriers to microbial transmission, likely due to restricted host dispersal. Although we observed a consistent distance‐decay relationship across the continent, our results suggest that the Mississippi River is associated with increased microbial species turnover, with dissimilarity across the river exceeding levels predicted by geographic distance alone. Furthermore, we identified specific microbial lineages that exhibit varying patterns of isolation by distance across the continent, suggesting a gradient in microbial transmission patterns ranging from lineages that are freely shared across space to those that are dispersal limited. Together, these findings suggest that the gut microbiome may act as a bioindicator of landscape‐level ecological connectivity, revealing discontinuities in microbial transmission associated with large‐scale landscape barriers even among closely related host populations that lack reproductive barriers.
n7f92f048f439: To understand the effects of climate change and other disturbances on ecosystems, methodologies capable of unravelling the complexity of biotic interactions are vital. Here, we present a dietary study on five passerines nesting in boreal forests: the crested tit Lophophanes cristatus, willow tit Poecile montanus, blue tit Cyanistes caeruleus, great tit Parus major, and pied flycatcher Ficedula hypoleuca. We used metabarcoding to describe their arthropod prey during the breeding season, and linked diets' properties with breeding success to understand birds' dependence on particular prey. The birds' diets contained hundreds of arthropod taxa, showing considerable richness and interannual variation. Most prey identities were resolved to species level. The most common prey were Lepidoptera, followed by Diptera, Coleoptera and Araneae. Dietary overlap was low to middling, conformed to temporal overlap, and fluctuated across the three studied years. Higher consumption of lepidopterans and their larvae was strongly associated with higher breeding success in blue tits and, to a lesser extent, great tits. In contrast, crested tits, willow tits and pied flycatchers had a more constant breeding success without relying on specific prey. The results suggest that the more recently settled blue tits and great tits are less capable of optimally utilizing the comparatively resource‐poor boreal environments. The apparent good adaptation to local foraging conditions contrasts to declining population trends in the Red‐Listed crested tits and willow tits. Our study highlights the complexity of arthropod communities and insectivore food webs, and showcase how molecular methods can be used to study ecological interactions.
n050ac2ccbcb2: Understanding how phenotypic plasticity and local specialization are shaped by gene flow and environmental heterogeneity requires natural systems that vary in both spatial isolation and environmental conditions across the landscape, yet such systems are uncommon. Naturally discontinuous inselbergs may provide this opportunity. Here, using populations of the inselberg‐specialist frog Leptodactylus lithonaetes, we evaluated whether habitat discontinuity translates into restricted gene flow and genetic structure and then tested how variation in connectivity and environmental heterogeneity shapes the balance between phenotypic plasticity and local specialization. We predicted that populations with higher environmental heterogeneity and higher gene flow would evolve plasticity in growth and development, whereas populations in more homogeneous environments and more genetically isolated would exhibit reduced plasticity and increased specialization. Using > 11,000 SNPs, we showed that the apparent habitat discontinuity among nine inselbergs spanning 300 km was reflected in a strong population structure and varying levels of gene flow among inselbergs, in an isolation‐by‐distance pattern. We then tested whether tadpoles alter their size or timing at metamorphosis to pond‐drying risk, and whether these plastic responses vary among populations with environmental heterogeneity (seasonality). Although tadpoles did not plastically accelerate metamorphosis under pond‐drying risk, the magnitude of body mass reduction under desiccation stress differed among populations, indicating developmental plasticity in body mass. Northern localities, exposed to greater environmental heterogeneity, showed greater survival and less body weight loss, resulting in higher tolerance to environmental stress than southern localities. Even in the absence of developmental acceleration, population‐level variation in responses to environmental stress is congruent with reduced plasticity, or increased specialization, in isolated populations exposed to less heterogeneous environments.
n460872390ada: The Antarctic region, a centre of biodiversity origin, influences deep‐sea ecosystems by supplying species to distant regions. Understanding the influence of Antarctic Upper Circumpolar Deep Water (UCDW) on deep‐sea eukaryotic diversity is therefore essential for outlining global biodiversity patterns. Our results showed the UCDW community exhibited ~1.5‐fold higher taxonomic and phylogenetic diversity than the Caroline Basin control community and contained a substantial proportion of unique taxa across multiple eukaryotic lineages. Source tracking using the available Southern Ocean surface‐water reference detected a 4.42% Antarctic‐associated contribution to the UCDW community. Indicators and generalists of the UCDW community shared > 97% sequence identity with Southern Ocean samples. The community analyses suggested that the Yap‐Mariana Junction choke point did not constitute a strong barrier to connectivity between adjacent basins, consistent with UCDW‐mediated dispersal into the Philippine Basin. The UCDW microbial dispersal into the Philippine Basin occurs through two potential routes: directly through the YMJ at 2000–3000 m and via upwelling across seamounts at 500–750 m. Governed mainly by neutral, dispersal‐driven processes, the UCDW community showed strong genetic exchange and connectivity. These findings suggest a role for deep‐water circulation in shaping the diversity and distribution of eukaryotes detected in western Pacific deep‐water samples.
n4385f8b6df39: Maps of the estimated root nitrogen concentration in the < 0.5‐mm‐diameter classes of 20 woody species based on the imaging spectroscopy using the shortwave infrared spectral region. See also the Commentary on this article by Rewald, 252: 1695–1699. Summary Tree fine‐root morphological, anatomical, and chemical traits are important to reflect belowground resource acquisition strategies to support tree growth, but their measurements involve several labor‐intensive and time‐consuming procedures. We examined the efficacy of visible (VIS), near‐infrared (NIR), and shortwave infrared region (SWIR) spectral reflectance for predicting a comprehensive set of fine‐root traits. Spectral features of fresh fine roots in 20 tree species were analyzed using three distinct spectral datasets: the VIS–NIR (458–960 nm), the SWIR (967–2391 nm), and the combined spectral region (full‐range; 458–2391 nm). The partial least square regression (PLSR) model using root spectral reflectance was developed to estimate nine functional root traits. Comparison of the models revealed that the prediction accuracy was higher when using the SWIR and full‐range datasets than when using the VIS–NIR dataset. The trait with the highest prediction accuracy was root diameter. The predicted multiple root traits successfully reproduced the ordination of the multidimensional trait space, exhibiting a pattern highly similar to that of the observed traits. This method can advance our understanding of multidimensional fine‐root trait spaces and resource strategies by enabling efficient measurement and spatial modeling of root traits across diameter classes.
n0c77b086b3db: Important processes taking place in the apoplast during plant–pathogen interaction identified by multi‐omics profiling of the apoplastic fluid. Summary The extracellular space in plant tissues, known as the apoplast, remains one of the least characterized cellular compartments. The apoplastic fluid, akin to mammalian extracellular fluid, serves as the primary interface between pathogens and their host. It allows the exchange of signalling molecules, coordinates host cell responses and enables the circulation of pathogen effectors that modulate the immune response. We describe here a comprehensive multi‐omics analysis of the apoplastic washing fluids content just 6 h after the onset of Arabidopsis thaliana infection with Botrytis cinerea, a fast‐killing necrotrophic fungus. By varying plant nitrogen nutrition, known to affect both plant defenses and pathogen virulence, we identify candidates that do not stand out under optimal conditions. Our analysis uncovers novel nitrogen‐dependent mechanisms that regulate both basal and early induced apoplastic immunity, revealing the presence of previously unidentified, potentially protective apoplastic metabolites as well as RAN GTPase, a nuclear protein, thereby offering new insights into early apoplastic immune responses. Résumé L’espace extracellulaire des tissus végétaux constitue l’apoplasme, un des compartiments les moins bien caractérisés. De la même manière que chez les mammifères, chez les plantes le liquide apoplastique constitue une des premières interfaces entre les agents pathogènes et leurs hôtes. L’apoplasme permet l’échange de molécules, la coordination des réponses des cellules hôtes, ainsi que la circulation des effecteurs des agents pathogènes qui modulent la réponse immunitaire de l’hôte. Nous avons réalisé une analyse multi‐omique détaillée du contenu de l’AWF 6 h après le début de l’infection de feuilles d’A. thaliana par le champignon nécrotrophe B. cinerea. En faisant varier la disponibilité en azote pour les plantes, qui module à la fois les défenses de la plante et l’agressivité des agents pathogènes, nous avons pu identifier des candidats qui n’apparaissent pas dans des conditions optimales de croissance. Notre analyse a permis d’identifier de nouveaux mécanismes azote‐dépendants qui régulent à la fois l’immunité apoplasmique basale et précocement induite, révélant la présence de métabolites potentiellement protecteurs non décrits jusqu’à présent, ainsi qu’une protéine impliquée dans le transport nucleo‐cytoplasmique de type RAN‐GTPase, offrant ainsi une nouvelle vision de la réponse immunitaire apoplasmique précoce.
nfabfd3ce4c37: Population structure and AVR gene presence/absence of 383 single‐spore isolates from the US Mo population. Summary We examined the frequency of and variation in eight avirulence (AVR) genes from 840 Magnaporthe oryzae field isolates collected from the Southern United States relative to rice resistance (R) genes deployed from 1959 to 2017. Little coding or noncoding variation was detected in AVR‐Pi9, AVR‐Pib, ACE1 and AVR‐Pizt, which correspond to R genes not used in the United States. In the United States, AVR‐Pik, corresponding to rice R gene Pi‐k alleles deployed at varying levels since the late 1960s, was present in 37% of the isolates over six decades. AVR‐Pita1, corresponding to Pi‐ta deployed in the late 1990s, reached a low point in the 5‐yr period following Pi‐ta deployment and then recovered to 99% in recent years. Our results suggest a fitness penalty for M. oryzae isolates carrying nonfunctional AVR variants and provide concrete data on how changes in plant R gene composition can impact pathogen populations. These findings will inform localized strategies for R gene usage and durable control of blast disease. AVR frequencies differ over time between United States and global samples for AVR‐Pik, AVR‐Pi9, AVR‐Pii and AVR‐Pita1. Further whole genome analysis including additional US samples is necessary to confirm whether the United States is a geographically isolated population.
n8b4ad4d39530: Oxygen pool accompanying the growth of a new Typha angustifolia rhizome through anoxic sediment. Summary Wetland plants must supply oxygen to their rhizomes and roots to maintain aerobic respiration despite soil anoxia. Excess oxygen can diffuse into the environment, strongly affecting rhizosphere biogeochemistry. This radial oxygen loss (ROL) has often been observed to increase in the daytime, perhaps supported by photosynthetic oxygen production and stomatal opening. However, dynamics in rhizosphere oxygen pools do not derive exclusively from diel cycles. Using oxygen‐sensitive planar optodes (and simultaneous leaf gas exchange measurements), we compared the timing and magnitude of variation in rhizosphere oxygen pools due to diel cycles vs root and rhizome development in the widespread aquatic macrophyte Typha angustifolia. Diel cycles drove only slight variation in oxygen pool sizes (c. 5% oxygen saturation). Strongly oxygenated regions – regularly 25–30% oxygen saturation – appeared as roots and rhizomes grew, and then disappeared after several days of maturation. Expansive plumes of oxygen also developed upon the emergence of lateral roots and persisted for several weeks. These results indicate that root and rhizome development are dominant determinants of ROL in T. angustifolia. Seasonal and environmental controls over timing of belowground development likely have strong implications for rhizosphere biogeochemistry ranging from microbe‐controlled decomposition to redox‐sensitive transformation of metals in natural and managed systems.
n7d964e8a4816: The TF BpERF3 positively regulates drought tolerance and activates POD‐associated stress‐response genes in birch. Summary Drought tolerance in plants requires rapid conversion of water‐deficit signals into protective transcriptional and epigenetic programs. Although ERF transcription factors (TFs) are central regulators of stress‐responsive gene expression, how drought‐induced kinase signaling is coupled to chromatin regulation and antioxidant gene activation remains unclear. Here, we identify the ERF TF BpERF3 as a phosphorylation‐dependent regulator of drought tolerance in birch (Betula platyphylla). Using transgenic and CRISPR‐Cas9 mutant lines, protein interaction assays, immunoaffinity fluorescent electrophoresis (IAFE)‐based interactome mapping, post‐translational modification analysis, reactive oxygen species measurements, and drought phenotyping, we dissected the regulatory mechanism underlying BpERF3‐mediated stress adaptation. We show that BpERF3 activates the peroxidase (POD) genes BpPOD3 and BpPOD4, which are required for its drought‐protective function. Mechanistically, BpSRK1 phosphorylates BpERF3 at Ser355, enabling phosphorylated BpERF3 to competitively engage the HDAC domain of BpHDA6 and restrict BpHDA6‐dependent histone H3.1 deacetylation. Consequently, H3.1 acetylation is maintained, chromatin relaxes, downstream stress‐responsive genes are activated, and drought tolerance is enhanced in birch. Our findings reveal a BpSRK1‐BpERF3‐BpHDA6‐H3.1 regulatory module that links drought‐induced phosphorylation to local chromatin activation and redox homeostasis, providing mechanistic insight into plant stress adaptation.
nb112899bba83: Temperature responses of photosynthesis, mesophyll conductance and stomatal conductance to water across Gossypium hirsutum cv Sicot 71, Gossypium arboreum, Gossypium bickii, Gossypium gossypioides and Gossypium sturtianum. Summary Mesophyll conductance (g m) limits CO2 delivery to Rubisco, yet its responses to temperature, heat and water deficit are poorly resolved in cotton (Gossypium hirsutum). We characterised photosynthetic and g m temperature responses in five Gossypium species, then examined cultivated G. hirsutum and the Australian native Gossypium bickii under combined elevated temperature and soil water deficit to link physiological responses with mesophyll anatomy. Plants were grown under controlled glasshouse conditions. We quantified g m using simultaneous gas exchange and online stable carbon isotope discrimination (Δ, ‰) and measured leaf anatomy. Across species, photosynthesis and g m exhibited broad thermal optima (33–36°C). In G. hirsutum, water deficit at control temperature reduced g m and induced thicker, more porous mesophyll and thicker cell walls, while assimilation declined only under combined heat and water deficit. In G. bickii, g m and assimilation remained stable under combined stress, and g m was stimulated by elevated temperature without anatomical adjustment. g m emerged as a stress-sensitive trait in cultivated cotton, whereas G. bickii exhibited stress resilience, with responses incompletely explained by anatomical acclimation. Further research on g m responses to environmental stresses and on the mechanisms underpinning these responses is required to inform model development and identify traits for climate resilient crops.
n7e133e5bf7dd: Regulation of Arabidopsis organ sizes by the TAS3‐ARF2‐GRFs regulatory network. Summary Plant organ size depends on the coordination of cell proliferation and expansion, a process regulated by numerous factors, including transcription factors and small RNAs. However, how different small‐RNA pathways are integrated with growth‐regulating transcriptional networks remains only partly understood. Here, we studied how the Arabidopsis TRANS‐ACTING siRNA3A (TAS3A)‐derived trans‐acting small RNA pathway controls organ size in Arabidopsis thaliana. We found that TAS3A overexpression increased leaf and floral organ size, whereas tas3a mutants showed reduced organ growth. We show that TAS3A acts by modulating AUXIN‐RESPONSE‐FACTOR2 (ARF2) activity and that plants expressing a trans‐acting siRNA (tasiRNA)‐resistant ARF2 allele showed reduced organ growth. In turn, ARF2 repressed several GROWTH‐REGULATING FACTOR (GRF) genes, including GRF3, which is a direct ARF2 target and is also controlled by microRNA miR396. Furthermore, uncoupling GRF activity from ARF2 repression was sufficient to increase floral organ size. Interestingly, whereas the TAS3A‐ARF2‐GRF module regulates leaf and petal growth predominantly through changes in cell proliferation, gynoecium growth involves a more complex balance between cell proliferation and elongation. Together, our results identify ARF2 as a central molecular node connecting tasiRNA‐ and miRNA‐dependent pathways and establish TAS3A as a key regulator of Arabidopsis aerial organ growth.
n21ec36c57c0e: The RING type ubiquitin ligase (E3), XBAT35.2, positively regulates FLS2‐mediated plant immunity against bacterial pathogens by modifying the ESCRT‐I subunits VPS28‐2 and VPS37‐1 with distinct ubiquitin chain types. Summary Sensing of pathogen‐associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) by pattern recognition receptors at the cell surface initiates the first layer of host immunity against invading microbial pathogens. In plants, the immune receptor Flagellin Sensing 2 (FLS2) perceives bacterial flagellin to trigger downstream signaling that culminates in PAMP‐triggered immunity (PTI). FLS2 protein levels are critical for effective PTI, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing its stability remain to be fully elucidated. Our previous work showed that the Arabidopsis Really Interesting Gene (RING) type ubiquitin ligase XBAT35.2 positively regulates plant immunity against bacterial pathogen Pseudomonas syringae pv tomato by promoting FLS2 stability. In this study, we demonstrate that XBAT35.2 interacts in vivo with two key ESCRT‐I complex components, VPS37‐1 and VPS28‐2. XBAT35.2 ubiquitinates VPS37‐1 with K48‐linked polyubiquitin chains, leading to its proteasomal degradation, and modifies VPS28‐2 with K63‐linked chains, reducing its interaction with FLS2. VPS37‐1 and VPS28‐2 play redundant, negative roles in FLS2‐mediated immunity by promoting vacuolar degradation of FLS2, displaying differential effects on distinct FLS2‐mediated immune responses. By targeting VPS37‐1 and VPS28‐2, XBAT35.2 intercepts this degradative pathway, thereby stabilizing FLS2 and enhancing host immunity. These findings uncover a novel regulatory circuit modulating FLS2 abundance and deepen our understanding of controlling the cell‐surface receptor homeostasis in plant immunity.
n146e1e2ad02e: Here, we reveal a PHYTOCHROME‐INTERACTING FACTOR 4 (PIF4)/ELONGATED HYPOCOTYL 5 (HY5)–xyloglucan xylosyltransferase 1 (XXT1)/XXT2 regulatory module that mediates xyloglucan biosynthesis in response to warm ambient temperature in plants. Elevated temperatures promote the conversion of phyB to its inactive form, releasing PIF4‐mediated transcriptional activation of XXT1 and XXT2, which encode key enzymes for xyloglucan biosynthesis. HY5 antagonizes this process by competing with PIF4 for promoter binding, thereby suppressing XXT1/XXT2 expression. nae0763f46661: Anisotropic guard cell wall stiffness enhances onion stomatal pore opening by increasing guard cell arc length. n7aea89ac771d: A holobiont‐level desiccation strategy in intertidal red algae. na4609eddcecb: Conceptual framework for partitioning the drivers of community stability. n551a1144d27b: We developed a new method to specifically track proteins moving through the main secretion pathway. nd0140d34f435: Multiple facets of Chlorella ohadii biological properties and potential as a research model and biotechnology platform. nc8f507760873: Tuberigen and antituberigen control of potato tuberization. nf9b0dd4c08c2: Grain protein content is usually measured on bulk samples, hiding variation between individual grains. n2c4b79c77f91: Cladogram of the streptophytes illustrating the diversity of apical growth mechanisms in this group. n7c407337856d: Mesocosm placement within the growing facility. Summary Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) show substantial genetic, trait, and functional variation within species. n7a0a361a8989: Reconstruction of leaf mimicry in fossil insects and plants and their familial diversity from the Paleozoic to the Cenozoic. ne545ba5e1b1c: Examples of hierarchical drivers of intraspecific variation in seed traits. n70c83c72ffff: Lyonia lucida and Lyonia fruticosa have translucent, unpigmented regions at the proximal end of the corolla (‘windows’). nfbefa6022c69: Hypothesized patterns of phytochemical differentiation between aboveground (leaves) and belowground (roots) organs along elevational gradients. We reveal that organs of the same tree tell distinct chemical stories, illuminating the chemical life of trees. 概括 植物产生多种代谢产物以抵御生物胁迫和非生物胁迫。然而，沿环境梯度对植物化学防御的定量研究主要集中在地上器官，而地下器官的变化规律至今尚不清楚。 为探究叶片和根系化学防御如何随生物与非生物条件的变化而改变，我们比较了跨越热带、亚热带和亚高山森林的海拔梯度上183个物种的非靶向代谢组学数据。 叶片和根系在不同海拔上表现出明显的化学组成差异，植物化学多样性从热带森林到亚高山森林呈下降趋势，这与植食性压力及土壤条件的变化相对应。这些模式表明，海拔梯度上生物与非生物压力的局部变化可能与化学多样性的梯度变化相关。我们还发现，不同器官之间的化学策略呈现出相反的模式。叶片化学组成从热带森林中以极性、快速周转、低成本的代谢产物为主，转向亚热带和亚高山森林中以极性较低、芳香性且能量成本较高的代谢产物为主；而根系则表现出相反的代谢调整趋势。 我们的结果表明，海拔通过器官特异性和环境依赖性的化学投入来筛选具有不同代谢组学特征的物种，这强调了整合地上与地下器官对于理解植物沿环境梯度的化学响应的重要性。我们发现，同一棵树的不同器官讲述着截然不同的化学故事，揭示了树木的化学生命图景。
n974806e695d7: Soil microbiome studies often define ‘core microbiomes’ using different operational criteria, including occurrence thresholds, abundance thresholds, or other selection methods. n64761aa22933: Overlapping niches and life habits of rootless vascular plants. Summary The evolution of roots was an instrumental event in the colonisation of land by vascular plants. Combinatorial analysis showed these alleles synergistically improve culm traits in their respective subspecies. Overexpression of STRONG3 enhanced lodging resistance without compromising grain yield. nc4bf0d2ffeca: A proposed model illustrating how CGE1 SUMOylation regulates chloroplast protein import and TIC‐associated machinery homeostasis. Summary In Arabidopsis, chloroplast protein import relies on the stromal cpHsp70 motor system, whose nucleotide‐exchange factor CGE1 is indispensable, yet its regulatory mechanism remains poorly defined. Loss of SUMOylation simultaneously strengthens the CGE1‐cpHsp70‐1 and CGE1‐TIC40 interactions, and overexpression of either cpHsp70‐1 or TIC40 in CGE1K214R‐complemented plants restores TIC40 and/or TIC110 levels and the photosynthetic phenotype. In conclusion, these findings reveal that SUMOylation of CGE1 plays an important role in regulating TIC complex abundance and precursor import efficiency through cpHsp70‐ and TIC40‐related routes. This study uncovers a SUMOylation‐mediated regulatory layer that fine‐tunes chloroplast biogenesis.

n9e2c3c8a0eb0: Schematics of ΔSPPbALE‐induced disruption of plant endomembrane trafficking impairs both preinvasive and postinvasive immunity against filamentous fungi and facilitates intracellular colonization by Plasmodiophora brassicae. Summary Plasmodiophora brassicae, an intracellular biotrophic protist that causes clubroot in crucifers, extensively alters the host endomembrane system for colonization. However, the molecular mechanisms and functions of effectors to achieve this remain poorly understood. n18966f8d0a1b: A workflow for better use and integration of taxonomic‐related information into ecological datasets. Summary Accurate taxonomy, including species identification and naming, underpins ecological inference, yet taxonomic information in ecological datasets is often inconsistently recorded or weakly standardized. With the increasing integration of ecological datasets across taxa and regions, datasets with poor taxonomic practices can hinder data exchange and propagate errors. We propose 10 rules to improve the storage and management of taxonomic information in ecological datasets. These rules draw on our experiences in plant ecology and taxonomy, but the conclusions may be generalized to other organisms and disciplines. They emphasize aspects from species identification to the permanent storage of verifiable records (e.g. voucher specimens) and include taxonomic standardization, nomenclature, validation, and updating. We also address the treatment of morphotypes and incomplete identifications, the use of automated name‐matching tools, and (meta)data standards. Closer collaboration between ecologists and taxonomists is key to ensuring more robust datasets. The application of these rules consumes more time and resources, but they enhance data quality and interoperability, saving time during data integration and improving the reliability and scalability of ecological research. Resumo Uma taxonomia precisa, incluindo a identificação e nomenclatura das espécies, é fundamental para a inferência em ecologia. Entretanto, as informações taxonômicas em conjuntos de dados ecológicos frequentemente são pouco padronizadas. Com a integração contínua de dados ecológicos entre diferentes grupos taxonômicos e regiões, a adoção de práticas inadequadas pode dificultar o intercâmbio de dados e propagar erros. Neste trabalho, nós propomos dez regras para aprimorar o armazenamento e curadoria de informações taxonômicas em conjuntos de dados ecológicos. Essas regras foram baseadas em nossa expertise em ecologia e taxonomia vegetal, mas suas conclusões podem ser generalizadas para outros organismos e disciplinas. As regras enfatizam aspectos que vão desde a identificação de espécies até o armazenamento permanente de registros verificáveis (por exemplo, espécimes‐voucher) e incluem assuntos referentes a nomenclatura, padronização, validação e atualização taxonômica. Também abordamos o tratamento de morfotipos e identificações incompletas, o uso de ferramentas automatizadas de correspondência de nomes e padrões de (meta)dados. Uma colaboração mais estreita entre ecólogos e taxonomistas é essencial para garantir conjuntos de dados mais robustos. A aplicação dessas regras demanda mais tempo e recursos, mas melhora a qualidade dos dados e a interoperabilidade, economizando tempo durante a integração de dados e aprimorando a confiabilidade e escalabilidade em ecologia. Con el aumento en la integración de bases de datos ecológicos de distintas taxones y regiones, los conjuntos de datos con prácticas taxonómicas precarias pueden propagar errores y dificultar el intercambio de datos. En este manuscrito, proponemos diez reglas para mejorar el almacenamiento y el manejo de información taxonómica en bases de datos ecológicos. Estas reglas se basan en nuestra experiencia en ecología y taxonomía de plantas, pero pueden extrapolarse a otros organismos y disciplinas. n693b26589216: For wintering and migrating birds, contamination from oil and other substances may delay arrival on the breeding grounds and lead to lower body mass upon arrival. These delays and losses of body mass could lead to smaller clutch sizes and lower propensity to renest. To determine potential effects of these consequences on breeding, we used an augmented version of an existing mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) reproduction model. By combining that reproduction model with the outputs of a previously developed migration and energetics model, we assessed carryover effects of simulated wintering ground oil spills on duckling production and other breeding season‐related population parameters. For simulated oil spills that occurred in January, reduced adult population and sublethal effects of migration delays both contributed to decreases in duckling production. For a simulated oil spill that occurred in March, sublethal effects from reduced body mass were the primary driver of decreased duckling production. By combining migration and energetics modeling with a reproduction model, this framework could provide the basis for a tool to generate quantitative estimates of lost reproduction resulting from carryover effects. Furthermore, this modeling framework could also be adapted for other avian species, facilitating assessments of reproductive loss in the context of Natural Resource Damage Assessments following contamination events.
nf6b90e8796c4: Habitat disturbances shape the diversity and composition of plant and animal species. It is important to distinguish between natural disturbances caused by megaherbivores and anthropogenic disturbances caused by human activity, as different disturbance regimes differently affect biodiversity. We assessed butterfly diversity with bait‐traps in primary forest with and without elephants, and in secondary forest characterised by previous human use and where elephants are currently present. In total, we activated 24 traps, eight traps per forest type. We found differences in the butterfly diversity and community structure depending on forest type and disturbance regime. The rather dense primary forest harboured a considerably higher proportion of dark‐coloured forest butterfly species than the secondary forest, particularly in areas with elephant disturbance. The secondary forest has higher butterfly species richness than the primary forest due to the occurrence of savannah species. Correspondence analyses clearly separated the three forest types with respect to community composition. Species occurring also in anthropogenic habitats were significantly more abundant in the secondary forest than in the two primary forest types. Our findings underline that forest type and disturbance regime shape butterfly diversity and community structure. Our study underlines that the effects of natural disturbances and human‐induced disturbances on butterfly diversity differ fundamentally. Natural disturbances such as by elephant activities seem to promote typical forest butterflies.
nbfd8f3a8385a: Coral bleaching and mortality are commonly associated with heat stress during marine heatwaves (MHWs), yet attributing these responses solely to heat stress may overlook the complexity of contemporary MHWs. Here, we document a severe MHW affecting a central Red Sea reef in mid‐2024 that coincided with repeated nighttime low‐oxygen events. By integrating satellite and in situ records of temperature, dissolved oxygen and wind, alongside repeated surveys of in situ nursery‐reared coral fragments, we document the temporal coincidence of these conditions with rapid coral bleaching and mortality. As temperatures approached and exceeded 33°C during the MHW peak, nighttime oxygen minima were extreme (down to 15.2–57.8 μmol O2 kg−1) and diel temperature variability diminished (down to 0.31°C–0.67°C), indicating a loss of nighttime thermal reprieves. Coincident responses of nursery corals were atypical, with transitions from healthy or bleached states to mortality occurring within 7–8 days. Bleaching and mortality also occurred across diverse coral species in nearby habitats after the MHW peak, with < 1% live coral cover documented eight months later. Sustained high temperatures, reduced vertical mixing and increased nighttime respiratory demand likely constrained oxygen availability, resulting in low‐oxygen extremes. We posit that similar compound MHW extreme events may have gone undetected in the Red Sea and elsewhere, potentially obscuring the contribution of co‐occurring low‐oxygen extremes to coral responses attributed to heat stress.
n86cfd716e572: The genus Lysimachia is taxonomically complex, especially in East Asia. We analyzed the complete chloroplast (cp) genomes of four Lysimachia species (L. acroadenia, L. leucantha, L. thyrsiflora, and L. arvensis). The cp genomes (153–155 kb) showed the typical quadripartite structure. Comparative analysis identified two highly variable regions, which are promising molecular markers. Most protein‐coding genes showed Ka/Ks ratios below 1, but rps12 and psaI showed elevated Ka/Ks ratios that require further validation using codon‐based selection tests. The Maximum likelihood phylogenetic tree confirmed the monophyly of Lysimachia. Importantly, L. thyrsiflora clustered within subgenus Lysimachia section Lysimachia, contradicting its traditional classification and suggesting a complex biogeographic history, potentially involving historical connections across the Bering Land Bridge. Divergence time analysis estimated the genus origin at approximately 33 Mya. Our results clarify the phylogenetic status of key taxa and provide essential genomic resources for future evolutionary and taxonomic research on Lysimachia.
nae9effd2d73f: From 3954 citizen‐science observations screened, we report novel cases of predation by omnivorous arthropods on velvet worms, including the first confirmed records for harvestmen and a cave wētā. Using photographic evidence derived from citizen‐science observations, we document multiple predation events involving harvestmen (Opiliones: Cranaidae and Triaenonychidae) and a cave wētā (Orthoptera: Rhaphidophoridae), encompassing both intraguild predation and higher‐order opportunistic predation within cryptic terrestrial habitats. These interactions represent previously undocumented trophic links between phylogenetically distant lineages and expand the known repertoire of omnivorous arthropods as predators of onychophorans. Our findings document a previously unrecorded vulnerability in Onychophora, a group traditionally regarded as specialized predators defended by an adhesive slime system, and underscore the trophic flexibility of arthropod predators operating within leaf‐litter and subterranean ecosystems. Collectively, these observations document previously unrecorded trophic links in cryptic environments and illustrate the value of natural history data and citizen‐science platforms for detecting rarely documented interactions.
nf72e2264740d: For species with limited mobility, leveraging highly mobile species through animal transport can provide a mechanism for dispersal and range expansion. As such, migratory birds may serve as vectors to disperse mobility‐limited species long distances to potentially novel geographies. To further document the potential use of migratory songbirds as vectors of animal transport for land snails, we provide two accounts of amber snails (Succinea sp.) attached to songbirds during post‐breeding migration. Both accounts took place in southwest Louisiana; the first instance occurred on a White‐throated Sparrow (Zonotrichia albicollis) and the second occurred on a Northern Waterthrush (Parkesia noveboracensis). Observations like these can improve our understanding of species interactions that may impact ecology, distributions, and life histories.
n75b689625142: Conservation biology has traditionally sought to justify public investment made specifically for biodiversity. I explore an alternative proposition: whether biodiversity can be co-produced through investments that society already undertakes for other public purposes. Using the Dutch Room for the River programme as a case study, I examine how autonomous grazing contributes to the long-term management and functional improvement of restored river wetlands created primarily to improve flood safety. Rather than evaluating autonomous grazing as a restoration philosophy, I analyse it as a management technology operating within contractual hydraulic boundary conditions defined by the national river management authority. This study demonstrates that self-organising groups of large herbivores can maintain floodplain vegetation within prescribed hydraulic limits whilst contributing to wetland functions and reducing the need for repeated mechanical intervention. Nationally standardised Dutch cost estimates indicate that vegetation management based predominantly on autonomous grazing costs approximately one quarter as much as management relying largely on repeated mowing and biomass removal. Biodiversity therefore emerges not as the primary objective of public investment, but as a valuable co-produced public good arising from the management of an engineered landscape. This study also illustrates the practical application of the Ecosystem Approach adopted under the Convention on Biological Diversity. Indeed, a clearly defined societal choice (flood protection) can be achieved through management that allows self-organising ecological processes to contribute simultaneously to economic efficiency, wetland functioning and biodiversity. It demonstrates that biodiversity need not always justify public investment, but can instead emerge as a valuable co-produced public good.
nb426c99e8eb0: IntroductionIn eusocial insects, the division of labor often entails significant mechanical costs for working individuals. In one-piece nesting termites, such as the Chilean endemic drywood termite, Neotermes chilensis, the colony's labor is performed by totipotent immatures that inhabit and consume structurally sound wood. This translates directly into severe mandibular wear. While the intense wood-processing activity of immatures has traditionally been viewed as an altruistic behavior that benefits the colony, recent evolutionary frameworks suggest it may represent a selfish developmental cost, the mechanical "price of adulthood", to fuel their own ontogeny into winged reproductives (alates). Conversely, alates, which can no longer molt to renew cuticular structures, must preserve their mandibles to excavate a nuptial chamber and found a new colony.MethodsTo investigate this, we quantified structural wear using a Mandibular Wear Index (MWI) and high-resolution scanning electron microscopy (SEM) across different developmental stages and sexes of N. chilensis (N = 147). To rule out size-related allometric artifacts, absolute mandibular dimensions were evaluated using an interactive Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) log -log model and estimated marginal means at a standardized common size (512.4 µm).ResultsOur results revealed no sexual dimorphism in wear but highly significant differences among castes that persisted independently of absolute mandibular size. Nymphs exhibited the most severe mandibular wear, consistent with their feeding activity to sustain energetic developmental demands. In stark contrast, swarmed alates possessed the sharpest, least worn mandibles. Primary reproductives and pseudergates displayed intermediate levels of wear.DiscussionThese findings reveal a caste-specific balance between mandibular wear in working immatures and preservation of mandibular structure in adult dispersers.

Abstract Resident songbirds in seasonal environments are adapted to fluctuating conditions and show marked phenotypic flexibility of metabolic rates. However, the potential strength and direction of selection for metabolic phenotypes may depend on the context of the seasonal and environmental conditions, which standardized metabolic rate is measured, and which life-history traits (i.e., survival and reproduction) are considered. To investigate how metabolic rates co-vary and to characterize individuals by a metabolic phenotype, we measured three different metabolic rates that we expected to be important for fitness – the maintenance metabolic rate (BMR), maximum cold-induced metabolic rate (M sum) and maximum exercise-induced metabolic rate (MMR) – in a population of blue tits (Cyanistes caeruleus) in southern Sweden. We then monitored different predictors of fitness for those individuals; apparent survival and breeding success. All three metabolic rates were positively related, and the relationship between M sum and MMR was positive independent of body mass. MMR was repeatable between seasons, suggesting consistent individual differences consistent with metabolic phenotypes. From breeding data, individuals with higher metabolic rates in spring were marginally more likely to return to breed the following year. However, high metabolic rates were associated with somewhat lower reproductive success. This study contributes to our understanding of how individual phenotypic variation and flexibility manifests in a population of temperate resident birds. While clear associations between metabolic rates and fitness remain elusive, our results provide tentative support for context-dependent selection on metabolic rates. Abstract Animal weapons often signal fighting ability, and signalling theory predicts that weapon size should reliably reflect weapon performance. Weapon loss and regeneration can disrupt this relationship by decoupling signal magnitude from functional capacity, but the consequences of such mismatches should depend on whether opponents can detect regenerated structures and whether signal reliability is tested during contests. We tested these hypotheses in the crayfish Cherax destructor by experimentally removing one chela from 40 individuals and comparing weapon morphology, strength, growth, swimming performance and contest outcomes with 40 control individuals after 12 months of regeneration. Regenerated chelae were smaller, more slender and weaker for their size than original chelae, demonstrating a decoupling between weapon size and strength. Despite this reduction in performance, regeneration imposed few detectable costs on body growth or swimming performance. Contest experiments revealed that weapon size alone predicted success in interactions resolved by signalling, whereas both weapon size and strength predicted success when contests escalated to physical combat. Consequently, individuals bearing regenerated weapons gained the benefits of enlarged weapons during signalling interactions despite possessing inferior weapons during fights. Our findings are consistent with the expectation that unreliable signals can persist when opponents do not detect reduced performance and only occasionally test signal reliability through escalation. However, additional experiments are needed to isolate the sensory mechanisms underlying receiver assessment and to directly test detection of regenerated weapons. nea9e68c64d0b: Soil organic matter (SOM) is a complex and dynamic substrate central to the functioning of terrestrial ecosystems. Because of its heterogeneity, SOM is routinely parsed into physical fractions with more uniform composition and behavior. Over the last several years, particulate (POM) and mineral‐associated (MAOM) organic matter have become the most widely adopted of these fractions, which has given the field a shared, comparable framework for resolving the first‐order heterogeneity within SOM. As fractionation has become routine, however, it has become clear that POM and MAOM identity alone cannot resolve the finer, second‐order variation that additional mechanistic inference requires. This is in part because the fractions are operationally defined composites, whose properties vary across composition, formation pathway, and behavior. Conceptualizing them as the terminal state of analysis collapses each fraction to its central tendency, flattening the distribution and obscuring the structure on which more complex questions depend. Here we propose embracing this within‐fraction heterogeneity rather than averaging over it, treating POM and MAOM as composite distributions whose internal structure underlies the variation in how they form, persist, and function. We suggest that this view can be operationalized via two complementary approaches: tailoring fractionation methods to target subpopulations most relevant to a question, and pairing fractions with orthogonal measurements. Together, these resolve the within‐fraction distribution that bulk measurements integrate over, narrowing the analysis onto the most explanatory slice of the bulk SOM. Similar to the original framework, we do not aim to prescribe a certain methodology, but rather a way of thinking about heterogeneity within SOM, in which a separation is justified by the understanding it produces rather than the data it generates. This way of reasoning allows POM and MAOM to continue linking organic matter to its functions, and in doing so supports more informed stewardship of soil carbon.
ne80abd45ecbc: Plants assimilate carbon through photosynthesis to support biomass production (BP), autotrophic respiration (R a) and the synthesis of non-structural compounds. Biomass production efficiency (BPE), the fraction of assimilated carbon allocated to BP, is one key factor influencing ecosystems' potential to store carbon. However, there is no consensus on the controls of BPE, and even the sign of its response to growth temperature is unclear. By means of statistical hypothesis testing using the largest observational dataset to date on annual BPE (n = 514 records) from evergreen and deciduous woody plants, we confirm earlier findings that BPE declines with stand age and is greater in deciduous plants. However, we also show that BPE declines toward more organic, sandy, or alkaline soils and increases with climatic aridity, while declining with warmer growing seasons and increasing with warmer winters. Such a dual temperature response is consistent with additional carbon costs due to the need for cold-hardening processes, and reconciles contradictory published reports of both positive and negative effects of temperature on BPE. Notably, our analysis provides novel evidence that BPE is significantly higher in species associated with arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi than in those associated with ectomycorrhizal (EcM) fungi and mixed EcM–AM associations. Our analysis explains the observed BPE patterns better than dynamic global vegetation models (DGVMs) from the TRENDY (Trends and Drivers of the Regional-Scale Terrestrial Sources and Sinks of Carbon Dioxide) project, which show a weaker correspondence with observations. In particular, our model captures reduced BPE in boreal regions, consistent with the predominance of ectomycorrhizal (EcM) species there. This study advances understanding of the global controls of BPE, and suggests a route toward the improved representation of plant growth in vegetation and land surface models.
n95de648de9ec: Soil invertebrates play a key role in ecosystem functioning, yet their monitoring remains constrained by labour‐intensive extraction and taxonomic identification procedures. Consequently, large‐scale and high‐frequency assessments of soil biodiversity remain difficult despite increasing demand for standardized monitoring tools. Here, we present an AI‐driven soil extractor that combines classical dry extraction with real‐time computer vision and deep‐learning‐based classification of soil microarthropods. Organisms are detected and classified while moving through the device, allowing automated quantification of taxon densities while individuals remain alive and available for subsequent analyses. System performance was evaluated using a validation framework that separately assessed AI classification accuracy, the integrated detection and transport workflow, and extraction performance relative to conventional Berlese funnels. Automated image classification achieved an overall accuracy of 80.9% (95% CI: 79.9%–81.8%; Cohen's κ = 0.767) when compared with expert image identification. Automated detections and manual identification of the same extracts showed high agreement in community composition, with a median Bray–Curtis similarity of 0.80, indicating limited mechanical bias introduced by specimen transport. Abundance estimates obtained with the automated system closely matched those produced by conventional Berlese extraction, with only minor taxon‐specific differences. Controlled experiments further demonstrated high mechanical reliability, with detection success exceeding 97% and transport success exceeding 92%. The system provides a scalable approach for quantitative monitoring of soil microarthropod communities while preserving live specimens for downstream analyses. By integrating extraction, image acquisition, classification and specimen collection into a single workflow, the AI‐driven soil extractor offers a practical tool for high‐throughput soil mesofauna monitoring.
n96a54e21ffa4: Environmental hypoxia at high elevations is linked to increased rates of gestational complications. Evolutionary adaptation to high elevation environments mitigates these complications across mammals, in part through changes in placental function that shape foetal growth potential in late pregnancy. We show that gestational hypoxia induced remodelling of the placental transcriptome in susceptible, lowland‐derived mice, but not in highland‐derived mice. A subset of this transcriptional plasticity displayed genetic assimilation, in which highland placentas expressed the induced value observed in lowlanders. However, we also found evidence that highland‐derived mice reversed some of the ancestral lowland responses to hypoxia. Specifically, gestational hypoxia tended to suppress metabolic pathways in the placentas of lowland mice, whereas these responses were attenuated in highland mice. This divergence was centred on mitochondrial metabolic pathways. More broadly, we show that both constitutive population‐level differences and remodelling of ancestral plasticity in the placenta tune expression within a stable transcriptional network architecture. Our results point to the developing placenta's metabolic responses to hypoxia as an early and developmentally specific functional target that likely contributes to pathologies associated with gestational hypoxia in humans and other mammals.
na1599e72684a: What makes a great review article in your field? n726c286fe79e: The application of hot product frameworks, such as value, inertia, visibility, and accessibility (VIVA) and concealable, removable, available, (abundance and accessibility), valuable, enjoyable, and disposable (CRAVED/CRAAVED), to illegal markets to understand the selection of wildlife products in them has gained momentum. Originally developed to study property crimes, these frameworks have been adapted for predictive analysis of wildlife product selection. However, their utility in explaining target selection and their empirical testability remain ambiguous. This study critically examined the use of the VIVA and CRA(A)VED frameworks in analyzing wildlife product selection for illegal markets. By reviewing peer‐reviewed studies and conducting a case study on Southeast Asian monitor lizards (Varanus spp.), we identified the challenges of applying these frameworks to real‐world contexts. These challenges are not merely methodological shortcomings of individual studies but reflect systematic difficulties inherent to applying these frameworks to wildlife contexts. The application of these frameworks to Southeast Asian monitor lizards confirmed that these issues transcend species groups. We also examined issues related to intraspecific variation in measures and variation between harvesters. Our analysis revealed complex interactions between attributes that influence wildlife product selection and identified key challenges to applying these frameworks, including incomplete data, inconsistent attribute measurements, and the dynamic nature of decision‐making during wildlife harvesting. A significant concern is the reliance on trade data, which are typically collected much later in the wildlife trade chain, to infer harvesting decisions. Moreover, we argued that target selection is not solely determined by product attributes. A more problem‐oriented and individualized approach that accounts for opportunity structures relevant to individual harvesters is needed to prevent aggregation fallacies. Thus, applying hot product frameworks to study the selection of target wildlife products cannot be quantitatively tested using an additive equation, and these frameworks should not be applied alone but situated within other theories of crime. Reflexión crítica de la aplicación de marcos de productos de moda para explicar la selección de objetivos de los productos de fauna Resumen Resumen. Hoy en día ha cobrado impulso la aplicación de marcos de análisis de productos de moda, como el de «valor, inercia, visibilidad y accesibilidad» (VIVA) y el de «ocultable, extraíble, disponible (abundancia y accesibilidad), valioso, agradable y desechable» (CRAVED/CRAAVED), a los mercados ilegales para comprender cómo seleccionan los productos de fauna silvestre. Desarrollados originalmente para estudiar los delitos contra la propiedad, estos marcos se han adaptado para el análisis predictivo de la selección de productos de fauna silvestre. Sin embargo, su utilidad para explicar la selección de objetivos y su capacidad de comprobación empírica todavía son ambiguas. Este estudio examinó críticamente el uso de los marcos VIVA y CRA(A)VED en el análisis de la selección de productos de fauna silvestre para los mercados ilegales. Revisamos los estudios sometidos a revisión por pares y la realización de un estudio de caso sobre los varanos del sudeste asiático (Varanus spp.) para identificar los retos que plantea la aplicación de estos marcos a contextos del mundo real. Estos retos no son meras deficiencias metodológicas de estudios individuales, sino que reflejan dificultades sistemáticas inherentes a la aplicación de estos marcos a contextos relacionados con la fauna silvestre. La aplicación de estos marcos a los lagartos monitor del sudeste asiático confirmó que estas cuestiones trascienden los grupos de especies. También examinamos cuestiones relacionadas con la variación intraespecífica en las mediciones y la variación entre los recolectores.…
na882ce9fab29: One important goal of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) aims to halt extinction of species and reduce extinction risk 10‐fold by 2050. To help ensure that the actions taken under the targets of the KMGBF contribute to reducing species’ extinction risk, the Species Threat Abatement and Restoration (STAR) metric was designed to enable science‐based target setting for species. STAR quantifies the potential contribution of threat abatement actions or habitat restoration to reducing species’ extinction risk in an area. To support the effective implementation of STAR, we developed a framework to move from determining the threat abatement component of STAR (START) using global data to calibrating START using local data to setting targets and calculating realized START scores to measure progress. The framework outlines the specific approaches that can be implemented to calculate these different START metrics. First, estimated START scores use global data to provide an initial indication of the species and threats expected to be present within an area. Then, calibrated START scores involve confirming the local presence of species and threats, and the locally verified data allow for setting robust threat abatement targets, which can be articulated as target START scores. Calibrated START can also inform both reactive and proactive threat management. Finally, changes in threat intensity are then monitored and used to calculate realized START. Achieving realized START requires actors to not only reduce existing threats but also prevent additional threats emerging within the area. This framework provides a means for all potential actors, working across varying spatial scales, to quantify, plan, monitor, and deliver interventions to address species threats and then report the impact of the interventions using a consistent method and metric that are comparable and aggregable across actors and locations. nc914147624ae: Large mammalian herbivores (LMH) play complex roles in shaping tree cover and composition in savannas by suppressing trees through browsing and reducing competition from neighbouring trees and understory vegetation. Across tree species, LMH exclusion increased growth but elevated water stress, particularly under dry conditions. Moreover, the tree species with the most acquisitive water‐use strategy was most susceptible to increased water stress and reduced carbon assimilation under exclusion. These findings indicate that although LMH limit tree growth, they also reduce water stress. Ultimately, interspecific differences in tree physiology will affect how savanna communities respond to interacting pressures from climate change and LMH declines.
n9912cd4c5143: Understanding the biogeography and genetics of the invasion of oceanic islands by pest species can provide insights into how to limit such incursions. Further, no significant genetic differences were detected between Stewart Island and mainland populations, indicating a close connection. Conversely, at the genomic level, the Chatham Island population was significantly different from the two other populations and this was attributed to probable founder effects. n5253b3223221: Long-distance dispersal sustains genetic diversity across populations and facilitates recovery from disturbance, and dispersal also may shape how ecologically important morphological traits shift in response to environmental change. nd2ac02cfeaff: Understanding the interplay between climate change and ecology is crucial when attempting to reconstruct the evolutionary history of species, as well as predicting how modern species may fare in light of current anthropogenic climate change and habitat destruction. Our results interpret both lineages of phenacodontid as frugivorous “mixed feeders” that likely incorporated a large diversity of plant species and tissues, while Sifrhippus shows strong evidence of frugivory. The results of our study detail how herbivorous mammals adapt to intensive climatic and environmental disruptions, hinting at possible responses of modern fauna to present and future anthropogenic climatic and environmental breakdown.
n2496c016f447: Coastal cities, endowed with abundant ecological resources and convenient transportation, are epicenters where the tension between ecological protection and economic development is most pronounced. The results indicated that the water yield (WY), soil conservation (SC), carbon storage (CS) and habitat quality (HQ) exhibited divergent temporal trajectories from 2000 to 2020, although localized improvements were observed in the peripheral zones of ring-shaped built-up areas and in coastal wetland regions. Based on the analysis of land use composition and spatial distribution in RPAs, we proposed specific ecological restoration strategies and spatial planning recommendations. This “past-future” framework overcomes the constraints of traditional RPAs and provides a novel perspective on the evidence-based land management in coastal city.
ncd0ade038f81: The Prairie Pothole Region (PPR) is a working landscape of grasslands, cropland, and wetlands that supports some of the highest numbers of breeding waterfowl, waterbirds, shorebirds, and grassland birds in North America. Our results demonstrate that waterfowl conservation in the PPJV benefits many species of birds; variation in benefits can be used to guide future conservation efforts to address gaps in protection.

Abstract Charles Elton proposed that species‐rich communities are more resistant to invasion, yet a well‐known paradox persists: native diversity suppresses invasion at small scales while correlating positively with non‐native species diversity at broad scales. Moving beyond native observed diversity alone to community completeness, defined as the ratio of native observed diversity to its specific species pool, may offer a potential framework to address this scale dependency. This is because the completeness index reflects the degree to which a habitat saturates its available niche space, shaped jointly by abiotic and biotic filtering in an origin‐blind manner. At small spatial scales, native observed diversity and dark diversity (suitable yet absent native species) are negatively correlated. This implies that high native observed diversity indicates high community completeness, leaving limited vacant niche opportunities for both un‐arrived native and non‐native species and thus reducing invasibility. In contrast, at large spatial scales, greater environmental heterogeneity can yield a vastly expanded regional species pool where dark diversity also accumulates more, potentially resulting in lower community completeness and heightened susceptibility. It should be noted that native community completeness, based on the extant species pool, fails to capture the niche spaces left by historical species losses—a gap tracked by temporal dark diversity dynamics—yet these hypervolume holes can instead be successfully exploited and predicted by non‐native community completeness. Following on this logic, I propose a Completeness‐Based Invasion Theory, which hypothesizes that community invasibility is inversely related to community completeness across spatial scales. While further empirical testing across diverse systems is required, measuring completeness alongside observed diversity may provide a novel, scale‐independent perspective to advance our understanding and management of biological invasions. Combining both native community completeness and non‐native community completeness to predict non‐native species invasions may currently represent the optimal approach. Abstract Under harsh environmental conditions, community assembly processes are expected to drive pronounced functional convergence, with communities dominated by stress‐tolerant species. Integrating local communities with their regional species pools enables evaluating environmental filtering and disentangling habitat‐specific assembly processes. To assess whether the strength and direction of environmental filtering in extreme habitats depends on regional climate and topography, we adopted a trait‐based approach on a relatively underexplored habitat such as inland limestone cliffs. To test whether limestone inland cliffs function as extreme habitats that filter regional species pools towards stress‐tolerant trait syndromes or alternative habitat‐specific assembly processes, we sampled vegetation on inland limestone cliffs along an aridity gradient in three study areas spanning different European biogeographic regions, namely Alpine, Continental and Mediterranean. We compiled regional species pools from the Global Biodiversity Information Facility and integrated them into trait‐based null models to compare observed community structure against expectations under stochastic assembly, using a combination of functional traits compiled from field measurements and from databases. Additionally, to assess whether community assembly rules are shared across regions or shaped by regional context and topography, we quantify trait‐based non‐random assembly and functional convergence across biogeographic regions and different cliff aspects. The results show that in inland limestone cliffs, extremeness is context‐dependent. It varies with the selected traits, intensifies in humid regions and weakens on pole‐facing slopes in dry regions. Cliff plants showed reduced plant height across all regions and aspects, whereas leaf dry matter content was higher and seed mass was lower under specific conditions. These patterns indicate non‐random trait distributions towards conservative leaf strategies and reduced plant size, while the prevalence of small propagules may facilitate colonization of suitable microsites for establishment, often scarce and spatially scattered. Functional convergence occurred in the Alpine region and on equator‐facing cliffs in the Mediterranean region, with slope and microtopographic heterogeneity showing limited effects. Overall, inland limestone cliffs showed evidence of non‐random trait assembly and localized abiotic filtering, suggesting that these patterns are context‐dependent.
