Making such data available and usable for managers and practitioners is a priority for coral reef conservation. Incorporación de la condición de los arrecifes a la planeación de la conservación para cumplir con los resultados de sitio bajo el Marco Mundial para la Biodiversidad Resumen Para alcanzar la Meta 3 del Marco Mundial para la Biodiversidad (GBF) de Kunming‐Montreal, la selección de áreas protegidas debe tener en cuenta el estado de los ecosistemas en los distintos emplazamientos, además del objetivo del GBF de cubrir el 30% de la superficie. Aplicar esta consideración a los ecosistemas de arrecifes de coral supone un reto, ya que los datos que describen su estado son pocos y están fragmentados. Por lo tanto, existe incertidumbre sobre la eficacia de los datos sobre el estado de los arrecifes de coral a la hora de establecer prioridades de conservación. Para abordar esta incertidumbre, evaluamos si la inclusión de datos sobre el estado de los ecosistemas modificaba las prioridades de conservación cuando el objetivo era proteger los arrecifes y cumplir la Meta 3. Analizamos varios conjuntos de datos estáticos y temporales modelados sobre el estado de los arrecifes de coral de la Gran Barrera de Coral y descubrimos que la inclusión del estado de los arrecifes alteraba significativamente las prioridades de planificación espacial (p <0.001), con efectos que variaban según el indicador de estado utilizado. Casi la mitad de los arrecifes que se consideraban prioritarios para su protección cuando se incluían los indicadores de estado pasaban a tener baja prioridad cuando se excluían dichos indicadores. Cuando ignoramos la información sobre el estado, no se alcanzaron los objetivos de conservación en aproximadamente el 22% de los hábitats de arrecifes una vez que se incluyeron las medidas de estado, lo que resalta cómo los enfoques basados únicamente en la presencia pueden sobreestimar los beneficios de conservación al considerar que los arrecifes en peor estado contribuyen en igual medida a la protección de la biodiversidad. Estas diferencias en las áreas prioritarias ponen de manifiesto la necesidad de desarrollar y utilizar métricas de estado eficaces para diseñar sistemas de áreas marinas protegidas para los arrecifes de coral a nivel mundial. Poner dichos datos a disposición de los gestores y profesionales, y garantizar que sean utilizables, es una prioridad para la conservación de los arrecifes de coral.
nd85f33289762: Understanding the impact of changing temperature on population densities is necessary to predict the likely impact of climate anomalies (e.g., marine heatwaves) or forecast distribution shifts under future climate scenarios. Population densities are often analyzed using spatio‐temporal models (STMs), which typically predict densities based on local habitat conditions while also estimating latent spatial and spatio‐temporal variation. Recent research extends STMs by also estimating density responses to habitat conditions at nearby locations using a “spatially distributed lag” (SDL) that averages habitat conditions in the vicinity of samples. Here, we extend the SDL by incorporating insights from diffusion‐enhanced STMs to simultaneously estimate spatially distributed and time‐lagged responses to nearby and past habitat conditions (a “spatio‐temporal distributed lag” STDL). We then use summer bottom trawl survey data from the eastern Bering Sea (1982–2024) to measure whether spatial and/or temporal lags are parsimonious when predicting population density from temperature anomalies for six ecologically important fishes. Results show that time‐lagged responses are parsimonious, positive, and substantial (correlation of 0.20–0.83 per year) for five species, and that density responses to temperature anomalies also diffuse outward over time for four species at 30–53 km per year. A self‐ and cross‐test simulation experiment shows that model selection can identify the appropriate model and that parameter estimates are approximately unbiased. We therefore conclude that temperature carryover effects arise in marine fishes and implement the method in the R package sdmTMB so that future studies can estimate nonlocal and time‐lagged responses when measuring density responses to habitat.
na6f8efeb497e: This study shows that stand development decreases soil nitrogen and phosphorus availability and results in a shift from nitrogen limitation to phosphorus limitation. In response, there was a clear transition from trees depending more on root nutrient scavenging to trees relying more on both nitrogen scavenging by ectomycorrhizal fungi and root phosphorus mining as stands developed. Abstract Soil nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) availability generally decrease with forest stand development, yet how tree species acclimate to this decline remains largely unclear. The functional coordination hypothesis proposes that trees concurrently improve leaf nutrient recycling and root nutrient acquisition to cope with nutrient deficiency. Conversely, the resource limitation hypothesis posits that trees prioritize either strategy, as simultaneous employment of both strategies is resource costly. To test these conflicting hypotheses, we leveraged a chronosequence of Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica stands with six age classes ranging from 16‐ to 62‐year‐old. We measured a comprehensive set of 70 plant and soil variables including needle nutrient retranslocation and resorption, and root architectural, morphological, physiological and mycorrhizal traits to assess the response of needle nutrient recycling and root nutrient acquisition to changes in stand nutrient status. Stand development reduced soil N and P availability and caused a shift from N to P limitation as evidenced by increasing needle N:P ratios and decreasing N:P‐acquisition enzyme ratios. There was no evidence of N or P retranslocation from old to young needles, and nutrient resorption efficiency was independent of soil nutrient availability, indicating that adjustments of needle nutrient recycling contribute little to mitigating nutrient deficiency. Root length density decreased exponentially with stand development, whereas cord‐forming ectomycorrhizal fungi (EMF), root phosphatase activity and rhizosphere effects on plant‐available soil P logarithmically increased, implying a shift from root nutrient scavenging to combined EMF nutrient scavenging and root P mining. Synthesis. Our findings suggest that tree species do not necessarily rely on both improved recycling and acquisition to acclimate to soil nutrient scarcity with stand development. However, trees can simultaneously depend on physiological adaptations of absorptive fine roots themselves, as well as on a constrained selection of EMF. This reveals that complex sets of adaptations, both root‐based ‘do‐it‐yourself’ and mycorrhizal‐based ‘outsourcing’, can be effectively used by trees to cope with changes in soil nutrient availability.
n8ed4edae1e01: Insect societies are characterised by a reproductive division of labour between queens that monopolise egg production and workers that perform all non‐reproductive tasks. The queen specialisation in egg laying is typically considered to be constitutive and independent of environmental conditions, but this common assumption was recently challenged by the finding that the presence of workers both induces and maintains the queen specialisation in several species of ants. However, the molecular changes that translate worker presence into queen behavioural specialisation remain unknown. To investigate the transcriptomic basis of the socially regulated specialisation of ant queens, we produced 93 individual brain transcriptomes from queens of the black garden ant Lasius niger that were experimentally maintained in different social environments. Our transcriptomic analyses revealed that 123 genes were differentially expressed between the brains of queens maintained with and without workers. These genes were enriched for processes related to brain energy metabolism and neuronal plasticity and signalling. By investigating the response of selected genes of interest to further manipulations of the social environment, we identified four candidate genes that fully mirrored the queen behavioural changes. Specifically, their expression changes in response to worker presence were reversible and they did not respond to mere cues of the worker presence. These candidate genes included the transcription factor Krüppel‐homologue 1 and other genes in the juvenile hormone and insulin signalling pathways, both known to regulate multiple aspects of division of labour in social insects. By producing a robust, well‐replicated and well‐controlled investigation of the transcriptomic basis of the behavioural specialisation of ant queens, this study provides a better understanding of the emergence and maintenance of reproductive division of labour in insect societies.
n1df470aaa7c7: Sexual selection via honest (costly) signals of fitness can generate patterns in immunogenetic diversity at the major histocompatibility complex (MHC). MHC diversity explains variation in immunocompetence—and therefore fitness—thus impacting the ability to generate honest signals. Differences in guppy (Poecilia reticulata) colour patterns can be driven by opposing selection pressures of predation and female mate choice, but the effect of parasitism has received less attention. By studying 21 wild guppy populations in Trinidad, we sought to quantify covariation among parasitic Gyrodactylus spp. infections, male sexual ornamentation (orange and black colouration) and genetic variation at the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) at both individual and population levels. We found population level support for a correlation between MHC diversity and Gyrodactylus prevalence, including an overall association between MHC supertype composition and prevalence. At the individual level, supertype (functional) diversity again emerged as a more informative measure than allelic richness alone. Predation was associated with Gyrodactylus prevalence and orange, but not black, colouration. Notably, some of these relationships differed between the individual and population levels. Further, much of this variation was explained by processes acting at a broader geographic scale within river drainages, which comprise divergent guppy lineages. These findings suggest that evolutionary history and processes such as genetic drift and gene flow contribute substantially to these relationships, but that ecological variation (i.e., predation) interacts with these processes. Our findings indicate that multi‐trait relationships between colour, immunogenetic diversity and infection are best examined within their broader evolutionary and ecological contexts.
n87045044542f: Climate change is driving increasingly frequent and severe weather events that can undermine the effectiveness of conservation interventions for threatened species, yet the extent and mechanisms of such impacts remain poorly understood. We assessed both peer‐reviewed and gray literature to determine how climate adaptation interventions have been affected by weather events across different land types, Australian bioregions, taxonomic groups, and intervention categories. Specifically, we evaluated 593 climate adaptation interventions for 145 threatened species in Australia. We found 36% of the interventions experienced impacts from weather events, with only 9% of these reporting positive outcomes, which were significantly associated with above‐average rainfall. Critically, our dataset was dominated by plant‐focused translocations, with drought and wildfire representing the primary stressors. Most taxonomic groups, despite being targeted by conservation interventions, experienced population declines and habitat loss following weather events. Inadequate mitigation of cumulative threats, such as grazing pressure and weed invasion, frequently exacerbated negative impacts and reduced the resilience of ecosystems to withstand and recover from weather impacts. Our findings suggested that although extreme weather risks have been recognized, they are not yet being systematically incorporated into the design and implementation of climate adaptation interventions in Australia. We recommend adopting adaptive and integrated management approaches to enhance climate adaptation success for threatened species, particularly by enabling the systematic management of multiple threats and facilitating flexible, evidence‐informed interventions in response to changing environmental conditions. Future research should prioritize adopting more rigorous, proactive experimental designs that bridge the gap between recognizing extreme weather risks and implementing robust mitigation strategies. Expanding the empirical basis for climate adaptation is also needed for less‐represented taxa such as reptiles, invertebrates, and freshwater fish, as well as in regions with limited data such as central and northern Australia where increased cyclone and flooding intensities are already occurring. Impacto de los fenómenos meteorológicos sobre la efectividad de las intervenciones de adaptación climática para las especies amenazadas Resumen El cambio climático está provocando fenómenos meteorológicos cada vez más frecuentes y graves que pueden socavar la eficacia de las intervenciones de conservación de especies amenazadas; sin embargo, el alcance y los mecanismos de dichos impactos siguen sin conocerse bien. Analizamos la literatura revisada por pares y la literatura gris para determinar cómo se han visto afectadas las intervenciones de adaptación climática por los fenómenos meteorológicos en diferentes tipos de terreno, biorregiones australianas, grupos taxonómicos y categorías de intervención. En concreto, evaluamos 593 intervenciones de adaptación climática para 145 especies amenazadas en Australia. Constatamos que el 36% de las intervenciones se vieron afectadas por fenómenos meteorológicos y solo el 9% de ellas registraron resultados positivos, los cuales se asociaron de manera significativa con precipitaciones superiores a la media. Es importante destacar que nuestro conjunto de datos estaba dominado por traslados centrados en las plantas, siendo la sequía y los incendios forestales los principales factores de estrés. La mayoría de los grupos taxonómicos, a pesar de ser objeto de intervenciones de conservación, experimentaron descensos de población y pérdida de hábitat tras los fenómenos meteorológicos. La mitigación inadecuada de las amenazas acumulativas, como la presión del pastoreo y la invasión de malezas, a menudo exacerbó los impactos negativos y redujo la resiliencia de los ecosistemas para soportar y recuperarse de los efectos meteorológicos.…
nc35559884222: Understanding drivers of plant rarity, especially for highly threatened and understudied tropical oceanic island flora, can improve conservation prioritization. Studies exploring trait–rarity relationships have the potential to identify species that may be more vulnerable, but inference is often limited by incomplete taxon sampling and failure to account for local ecological context. We used the complete Kauaʻi single‐island endemic angiosperm flora (240 taxa), combining known population sizes and robust population estimates determined for International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List of Threatened Species assessments, and compiled data for 42 plant traits while accounting for elevation and habitat type to explore trait–rarity relationships. We tested for phylogenetic signals, accounted for correlation and log10‐transformed continuous trait data, and implemented phylogenetic linear models with a continuous response (log10(n + 1), where n is the population size) in the phylolm R package. Discrete variables were treated as fixed effects. We also tested multitrait models and individual confounding traits. We found that shorter species, species with shorter leaves, species with lower seed mass, and species with lower initial seed germinability were significant predictors of rarity. Species occurring at lower elevations and across narrower elevational ranges also tended to have smaller populations. Importantly, elevation influenced trait–rarity relationships, with plant height showing different relationships with rarity across elevation classes. Our findings demonstrated that traits associated with rarity are not universal predictors but context‐dependent indicators that may aid conservation prioritization. More broadly, our study highlights the value of more complete sampling and incorporation of local ecological context for trait‐based assessments of rarity, particularly for threatened oceanic island floras. Importancia del contexto ecológico en las relaciones característica‐rareza inferidas a partir de la flora angiosperma endémica de una sola isla Resumen Comprender los factores que determinan la rareza de las plantas, especialmente en el caso de la flora de las islas oceánicas tropicales, la cual está sumamente amenazada y poco estudiada, puede mejorar la priorización de la conservación. Los estudios que exploran las relaciones entre características y rareza tienen el potencial de identificar especies que pueden ser más vulnerables, pero las conclusiones suelen verse limitadas por un muestreo incompleto de los taxones y por no tener en cuenta el contexto ecológico local. Utilizamos la flora completa de angiospermas endémicas de la isla de Kauaʻi (240 taxones) junto con los tamaños de población conocidos y las estimaciones poblacionales robustas determinadas para las evaluaciones de la Lista Roja de Especies Amenazadas de la Unión Internacional para la Conservación de la Naturaleza (UICN) y recopilamos datos sobre características botánicas, considerando la altitud y el tipo de hábitat, para explorar las relaciones entre las características y la rareza. Comprobamos la presencia de señales filogenéticas, tuvimos en cuenta la correlación y los datos de rasgos continuos transformados en log10 e implementamos modelos lineales filogenéticos con una respuesta continua (log10 (n+1), donde n es el tamaño de la población) en el paquete phylolm de R. Las variables discretas se trataron como efectos fijos. También analizamos modelos multicaracterísticos y rasgos de confusión individuales. Observamos que las especies más bajas, las de hojas más cortas, las de menor masa de semillas y las de menor capacidad de germinación inicial de las semillas eran predictores significativos de la rareza. Las especies que se dan a menor altitud y en rangos altitudinales más estrechos también tendían a tener poblaciones más pequeñas.…
nbc0e7291593d: Periodically driven systems are ubiquitous in nature, and their stability against perturbations such as the introduction of a novel pathogens or invasive species is often a major concern. To better understand and control these systems, it is common to assess the sensitivity to changes in the model parameters of stability threshold quantities such as the basic reproduction number R0$$ {R}_0 $$, or the Floquet multiplier Λ$$ \Lambda $$, which determines stability against invasion of the disease/invader‐free system. However, traditional methods often assume that these parameter changes are permanent and constant in time, so they may over‐ or underpredict the cost‐effectiveness of management activities that can only be maintained for a limited time during each period, such as culling when most individuals are at an especially vulnerable life‐stage. Moreover, they cannot highlight important time junctures in the model dynamics. In this article, we address this problem by providing efficient algorithms to compute the sensitivities of objectives like Λ$$ \Lambda $$ and R0$$ {R}_0 $$ to periodic, time‐localised perturbations in the model parameters. These sensitivities provide information about when during each period interventions should have the largest effect on the objective, and can also be used to calculate the sensitivities to more general periodic perturbations. Hence, this article extends previous work on time‐dependent sensitivity analysis (TDSA) to a new class of problems relevant to stability analysis. Using empirically parameterised models for Lyme disease and hantavirus, we demonstrate that TDSA can provide useful and sometimes surprising insights that nonetheless have intuitive biological interpretations. Specifically, we find that culling at the optimal times of susceptible and infected non‐human hosts has additive effects in the hantavirus model, but opposite and nearly cancelling effects in the Lyme disease model, so that indiscriminate culling is predicted to be effective for hantavirus but ineffective for Lyme disease.
nf0e562b0f613: The Red List Index (RLI) is a key indicator for global biodiversity targets, but its application to freshwater fishes has been limited by infrequent reassessment and sparse monitoring data. To address this gap, we developed the first comprehensive RLI for freshwater fishes of the Western Palearctic (Europe, West Asia, and North Africa), based on two comparable global assessment rounds. We reconciled taxonomy, classified category changes as nongenuine (reflecting taxonomic revision or improved knowledge) or genuine, and calculated RLIs with bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals. Of 1,157 native, described species, 727 (63%) had two comparable assessments and formed the index. The RLI declined across the region (−2.4%), with subregional declines ranging from −0.8% in West Asia to −7.1% in North Africa; genuine declines outnumbered improvements by approximately 6:1 and included losses to extinct in the wild or possibly extinct. Most species showed no change or a nongenuine change. The main constraint on the trend was not data deficiency (eight species) but the absence of a comparable earlier assessment for 337 species recently assessed. Of these species, the assessments showed that 163 were threatened and concentrated in West Asia, and coverage was lowest in West Asia (51%) and for small‐bodied, range‐restricted families. The index should therefore be read as a regional benchmark and not as a test of the RLI's sensitivity because the true number of genuine changes that should have occurred is unknown. Building on this analysis, we developed a prioritized, data‐informed agenda for strengthening future iterations: completing a second assessment of the already‐threatened species currently outside the trend, focusing the resurvey on under‐covered subregions and families, and matching monitoring technique to taxon. Documented recoveries show that targeted conservation can reverse declines, often in data‐poor areas, but without such effort, both decline and recovery of these faunas will be detected slowly. Índice de la Lista Roja de peces de agua dulce del Paleártico occidental Resumen El Índice de la Lista Roja (RLI) es un indicador clave para los objetivos mundiales de biodiversidad, pero su aplicación a los peces de agua dulce se ha visto limitada por la escasa frecuencia de las reevaluaciones y la escasez de datos de seguimiento. Para subsanar esta carencia desarrollamos el primer RLI exhaustivo para los peces de agua dulce del Paleártico occidental (Europa, Asia Occidental y el norte de África), basado en dos rondas de evaluación global comparables. Conciliamos la taxonomía, clasificamos los cambios de categoría como no genuinos (que reflejan una revisión taxonómica o un mayor conocimiento) o genuinos, y calculamos los RLI con intervalos de confianza del 95% obtenidos mediante el método bootstrap. De las 1,157 especies autóctonas descritas, 727 (63%) contaban con dos evaluaciones comparables y formaron parte del índice. El RLI disminuyó en toda la región (–2.4%), con descensos subregionales que oscilaron entre el –0.8% en Asia Occidental y el –7.1% en el norte de África. Los descensos genuinos superaron a las mejoras en una proporción de aproximadamente 6:1 e incluyeron pérdidas por extinción en estado silvestre o posible extinción. La mayoría de las especies no mostraron cambios o presentaron un cambio no genuino. La principal limitación de la tendencia no fue la falta de datos (8 especies), sino la ausencia de una evaluación anterior comparable para 337 especies evaluadas recientemente. De estas especies, el RLI reveló que 163 se encontraban amenazadas y concentradas en Asia occidental, y que la cobertura era menor en esta zona (51%) y para el caso de las familias de pequeño tamaño y área de distribución limitada. Por lo tanto, el índice debe interpretarse como un punto de referencia regional y no como una prueba de la sensibilidad del RLI, ya que se desconoce el número real de cambios genuinos que deberían haber ocurrido.…
n96188a094773: IntroductionBamboo exhibits a complex taxonomy due to polyploidy, hybridisation, and long flowering periods, which complicate species identification. Traditional morphological taxonomy often struggles with limited diagnostic traits and considerable phenotypic variability, leading to taxonomic ambiguities and misinterpretations. The convergence of similar traits among unrelated species further complicates phylogenetic classification. To address these challenges, integrative taxonomic approaches are needed to combine morphological, molecular, and ecological data for accurate bamboo classification. This review synthesises the current status, recent advances, and emerging trends in molecular identification and DNA barcoding of bamboo, highlighting their potential to improve taxonomy, conservation, and the sustainable utilisation of bamboo genetic resources.MethodTo provide a framework for the review, a scientometric analysis was performed using bibliographic records.ResultsThe review suggests that no single marker or combination of markers can currently serve as a universal barcode across bamboo. The performance of commonly used markers such as ITS, matK, rbcL, psbA-trnH, rps16-trnQ, and alternative plastid regions provides valuable insights into species identification. Comparative evidence indicates that barcode performance is strongly marker- and lineage-dependent. These markers have improved plant taxonomy by providing more reliable species identification than traditional morphological methods.DiscussionDNA barcoding has been effectively used to understand complex species relationships and identify cryptic species that are difficult to distinguish morphologically. Furthermore, next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies have transformed genomic data acquisition, enabling species discrimination. Integrating machine learning with DNA barcoding further improves species identification accuracy and shows promise for improving conventional methodologies in bamboo systematics. However, the application of ML and NGS in bamboo is still in its early stages and will require substantial work on bamboo databases to achieve greater accuracy.
n7223340e883d: Sociality can improve access to information, cooperation, collective defense, parental care, collective decision-making, and social buffering, but it can also intensify competition and pathogen transmission, spread outdated information, and create dependence on particular partners, roles, or traditions. In this article, we propose the Intermediate Social Resilience Hypothesis (ISRH), which predicts that, under specified conditions, population resilience may be greatest at an intermediate value of a defined social dimension. We do not rank all animal societies on a single universal scale. Instead, low, intermediate, and high values must be defined within a measurable dimension, such as group size, cohesion, network connectivity, cooperative effort, or reliance on social information, and within a biologically comparable system. Resilience must likewise be specified as resistance, recovery, temporal stability, or persistence under a defined form and scale of environmental change. The distinctive contribution of the ISRH is not simply the recognition that sociality can generate both benefits and costs, but the explicit prediction that their balance can, under identifiable conditions, produce a testable intermediate maximum in population resilience. An intermediate optimum is expected only when social benefits initially increase but eventually saturate, whereas one or more relevant social costs continue to rise. Environmental harshness, variability, unpredictability, and the flexibility, modularity, redundancy, or multilevel organization of social systems may shift, flatten, or eliminate this relationship. The hypothesis generates two falsifiable predictions that can be tested through comparative, longitudinal, experimental, phylogenetic, network, and population-monitoring approaches. By integrating behavioral ecology, social evolution, resilience theory, and conservation, the framework explicitly recognizes the multidimensional nature of animal social systems while providing explicit criteria for distinguishing support for the ISRH from monotonic, threshold, flat, or context-dependent alternative relationships.
ne5f120c151b5: Wildlife damage is often expected to push national park residents toward new sources of income, but the appraisals that turn damage into a willingness to move into tourism remain unclear. Drawing on protection motivation theory and questionnaire data from 513 residents in and around the Wuyishan City section of Wuyishan National Park, China, this study distinguishes perceived tourism adaptive efficacy from tourism self-efficacy and examines how these two beliefs relate to intentions to shift household livelihoods toward tourism. Greater perceived wildlife damage was related to stronger threat appraisal of traditional livelihoods. Residents who perceived greater livelihood threat also reported stronger transition intentions and were more likely to view tourism as a workable livelihood alternative. However, no clear relationship emerged between livelihood threat and tourism self-efficacy, although both adaptive efficacy and self-efficacy were positively related to transition intention. As a moderator, perceived tourism development opportunity was more relevant to adaptive efficacy than to self-efficacy. When residents perceived greater tourism opportunities, the positive relationship between livelihood threat and adaptive efficacy was stronger, as was the corresponding indirect relationship with transition intention. In contrast, perceived opportunity made little difference to the relationship involving self-efficacy. These findings suggest that livelihood threat was associated with greater perceived usefulness and feasibility of tourism without a corresponding association with residents’ confidence in their own ability to engage in tourism activities. Policies aimed at encouraging livelihood diversification in national park communities may therefore need to combine the creation of tourism opportunities with training, skills development, and other forms of support that strengthen residents’ capacity to participate.
n3dde51d8a05b: This study reveals that host trophic strategy, not shared seasonality, drives gut microbiota plasticity in sympatric rodents. Herbivorous voles show tight diet–microbiome coupling; granivorous gerbils exhibit functional stability. This highlights gut microbiota as a potential key mechanism for niche differentiation and coexistence. Abstract The coexistence mechanisms of sympatric species have long attracted widespread research attention. However, it remains unclear whether sympatric species experiencing the same seasonal conditions exhibit convergent or host‐specific gut microbiota responses. We compared the herbivorous Brandt's vole (Lasiopodomys brandtii) and the granivorous Mongolian gerbil (Meriones unguiculatus), two sympatric rodent species with divergent trophic strategies inhabiting the grasslands of Inner Mongolia, China. By integrating plant DNA metabarcoding, gut microbiota profiling and microbial functional output analyses across seasons, we investigated seasonal dietary–microbiome associations. Our results revealed that although seasonal dietary variation affects the composition of the host gut microbiota, the taxonomic and functional plasticity of gut microbiota is strongly influenced by host trophic strategies. Brandt's voles maintained a fermentation‐oriented microbiota tightly coupled with seasonal shifts in Poaceae and Cyperaceae intake, exhibiting coordinated changes in microbial taxa, short‐chain fatty acid production and cellulase activity. In contrast, Mongolian gerbils exhibited substantial seasonal dietary turnover between Chenopodiaceae and Caragana plants, while maintaining comparatively stable microbial functional outputs, suggesting metabolic buffering. Host trophic strategy, rather than shared environmental seasonality, is related to the strength and functional consequences of the coupling between diet and microbiome. Our results emphasize the gut microbiome as a potential key mechanism underlying trophic niche differentiation and ecological coexistence in wild mammalian communities.
n3235ec97f1d8: Biological invasions on islands provide a natural framework to study how dispersal and connectivity influence evolutionary and ecological processes. The avian nest parasitic fly, Philornis downsi—first recorded in Darwin's finch nests in 1997—causes high mortality in endemic land birds, yet its inter‐island and sex‐specific patterns of dispersal and genetic structure remain poorly understood. We use low‐coverage whole genome sequencing to investigate genome‐wide patterns of genetic diversity, directional migration and effective population size in P. downsi across five major Galápagos Islands and its native range in mainland Ecuador. We find evidence for a genetic bottleneck in the Galápagos, isolation by distance, and evidence that the island closest to the Ecuadorian mainland, San Cristóbal, is genetically divergent from the other four islands sampled, despite retaining the highest genetic diversity. No evidence was found for sex‐biased dispersal; however, sex‐biased genetic structure was detected using only markers from inferred autosomal scaffolds. We found asymmetric gene flow with higher migration rates from San Cristóbal westward to the other islands, matching the direction of both southeast trade winds and major cargo shipping routes. Our results suggest both natural and human‐mediated colonisation of P. downsi from the mainland through San Cristóbal to the other islands, followed by high inter‐island dispersal among closely situated sink islands. Our findings are critical for prioritising islands for control strategies that will reduce P. downsi impacts on vulnerable endemic birds and underscore the value of understanding directional migration patterns for managing invasive species in metapopulations.
n6a804aa06e3a: Controlling invasive species is costly and difficult but can have major ecological, economic, and health benefits. Researchers commonly compare the efficacy of specific control methods. However, invasive species control programs vary greatly in overarching goals and often occur over large areas, long timeframes, and varied environmental and social contexts. The success of these programs likely hinges on factors including organizational structures, concurrent restoration activities, geographic and temporal scope of control, and the invasive species’ biology. To enable assessment of the relative influence of these common features, we propose clearer definitions of success in invasive species control and explicit comparisons among control programs. Post hoc assessment of existing programs’ success will complement system-specific studies to guide strategies that work in real-world situations.
nf6ca3b58ab9a: Vessel strikes threaten many large whale species. Managers employ several mitigation measures to reduce vessel strike risk, including establishing or modifying vessel routing measures, such as shipping lanes. However, most studies utilized to inform the configuration of shipping lanes only consider a limited number of potential lanes, and in many cases, the criteria used to generate the lanes are unclear. We developed an approach to design, modify, or evaluate shipping lanes that involves clearly defining the objectives of the lanes and using the k least‐cost path (KLCP) algorithm, which identifies the KLCPs between two points on a cost surface, to identify all lanes that meet the objectives. We applied our approach to evaluate recommended shipping lanes in Cape Cod Bay, Massachusetts (United States), and off the Atlantic Coast of the southeastern United States with respect to the risk of vessel strikes to North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) and the time it takes vessels to travel the lanes. We identified all lanes with a risk of right whale strikes and a travel time less than or equal to that of the recommended lanes using the KLCP algorithm. In most cases, the lanes identified had similar spatial configurations to the recommended lanes and reduced the risk of strikes by <15%, which indicates that the existing recommended lanes are adequately, but not optimally, designed to reduce strike risk and travel time relative to potential alternative lanes. Our approach applying the KLCP algorithm provides a thorough, objective, and transparent way to identify vessel routing configurations that minimize whale–vessel strikes and meet other objectives. Reducción de las colisiones entre ballenas y embarcaciones mediante la planificación de rutas de tráfico marítimo con múltiples objetivos Resumen Las colisiones con embarcaciones suponen una amenaza para muchas especies de ballenas de gran tamaño. Los responsables aplican diversas medidas de mitigación para reducir el riesgo de la colisión, entre ellas el establecimiento o la modificación de medidas de trazado de rutas marítimas, como las rutas de navegación. Sin embargo, la mayoría de los estudios utilizados para definir la configuración de las rutas de navegación solo tienen en cuenta un número limitado de rutas potenciales y, en muchos casos, los criterios empleados para generarlas no están claros. Desarrollamos un enfoque para diseñar, modificar o evaluar rutas marítimas que consiste en definir claramente los objetivos de las mismas y utilizar el algoritmo k de las rutas de menor coste (KLCP), que identifica las KLCP entre dos puntos en una superficie de costos, con el fin de determinar todas las rutas que cumplen dichos objetivos. Aplicamos nuestro enfoque para evaluar las rutas marítimas recomendadas en la bahía de Cape Cod, en Massachusetts (Estados Unidos), y frente a la costa atlántica del sureste de Estados Unidos, con la consideración del riesgo de colisiones de buques con las ballenas francas del Atlántico Norte (Eubaleana glacialis) y el tiempo que tardan los buques en recorrer dichas rutas. Identificamos todas las rutas con riesgo de colisiones con ballenas francas y un tiempo de travesía inferior o igual al de las rutas recomendadas utilizando el algoritmo KLCP. En la mayoría de los casos, las rutas identificadas presentaban configuraciones espaciales similares a las de las rutas recomendadas y reducían el riesgo de colisiones en menos del 15%, lo que indica que las rutas recomendadas existentes están diseñadas de forma adecuada, aunque no óptima, para reducir el riesgo de colisiones y el tiempo de travesía en comparación con posibles rutas alternativas. Nuestro enfoque, basado en la aplicación del algoritmo KLCP, ofrece una forma exhaustiva, objetiva y transparente de identificar configuraciones de rutas para buques que minimicen las colisiones entre ballenas y buques y cumplan otros objetivos.
nfc7c6c4d2934: Urban environments expose wildlife to anthropogenic hazards, including materials capable of causing physical injuries. Among urban birds, the rock pigeon (Columba livia) is highly adapted to urban environments. However, frequent reports of digit entanglement and foot deformities in these environments suggest that urban conditions expose birds to foot injuries. Despite widespread observations of “string foot”, quantitative assessments of deformity prevalence and severity across urban land-use types remain limited, particularly within African cities. This study assessed the prevalence and severity of foot deformities in rock pigeons across three land-use zones in Katima Mulilo, Namibia: the Central Business District (CBD), market areas, and residential areas. A total of 300 pigeons were visually inspected during systematic field surveys. Foot deformities were recorded as present or absent and classified into three severity levels (mild, moderate, severe). Forty-six (15.3%) pigeons exhibited foot deformities. The prevalence of foot deformities varied significantly among land-use categories, with the highest recorded in the residential areas (22.5%), followed by the CBD (12.4%) and least in the market areas (10.4%). Moderate deformities were the most prevalent injury category (60.9%), followed by severe (23.9%) and mild deformities (15.2%). Pigeons observed in residential areas had significantly higher odds of deformities compared with those in the CBD (OR = 2.05, p = 0.044). Fibrous wastes, which constitute the important potential sources of entanglement hazard, were prevalent in the environment of pigeons. Results of this study suggest that foot injury in urban rock pigeons varied across land-use types and highlight the potential role of human-derived materials on pigeon health in urban areas. Targeted management of fibrous wastes in the CBD and residential areas is recommended to reduce entanglement-related foot deformities, with emphasis on improved local waste handling and disposal behavior.
n8b28d1883135: Coral reefs are undergoing profound compositional changes driven by climate change, disease, and chronic human disturbance. Coral cover is the primary metric used to track reef condition, but it often fails to capture the contributions of different coral species to reef carbonate production, structural complexity, and associated biodiversity. Here, I review evidence showing that global change disproportionately removes competitively dominant and architecturally complex corals, driving non‐random changes and coral community homogenisation. These changes erode reef functionality, even when overall cover is maintained. Species‐specific contributions to calcification and structural complexity span orders of magnitude, such that targeted losses of framework‐building taxa collapse carbonate budgets and habitat architecture in ways not predictable from cover trends. These structural changes cascade through associated communities, undermining functional diversity and the ecosystem processes on which reef resilience depends. Critically, rebounds in coral cover frequently reflect the colonisation by fast‐growing opportunistic species, which yield slow or absent recovery of physical functionality, while reassembly and the re‐establishment of large, structurally complex colonies (and the physical functionality they provide) might lag by decades. Furthermore, as mass disturbance events occur at ever‐shorter intervals, recovery windows close before reef‐building potential and complexity can be fully restored. Monitoring, management, and restoration should therefore focus on trait‐ and species‐explicit assessments that prioritise protection and restoration of keystone reef‐builders, target sites with high functional potential, and reduce stressors at appropriate scales. Integrating functional metrics into policy and restoration planning is essential to safeguard reef geomorphic and ecological services under continued global change.
n311b75e6d0b9: Climate change and overexploitation are increasingly threatening sharks, with pelagic species among the most affected. We conclude by highlighting that the translation of this knowledge into practice requires engagement with the scientific and management bodies responsible for evaluating the evidence, advising decision‐makers, and implementing shark conservation measures.
n0edafbbe2040: IntroductionScientific understanding of the spatio-temporal evolution of Production-Ecological-Living Spaces (PELS) and their driving factors provides theoretical support and practical guidance for territorial spatial planning. Abstract Climate change is driving shrub encroachment and treeline advance in the Arctic, increasing inputs of plant‐derived carbon (C) to soil. However, counter to expectation, glucose addition did not generally strengthen selective microbial N‐mining, likely because microbial use of N‐rich SOM was already near its stoichiometric limit (set by the lowest possible C:N ratio of organic compounds). This was with the exception of N‐fertilised soils, where glucose addition primed soil N mineralisation (up to +250%), resulting in intensified selective microbial N‐mining, with an effect size that tended to strengthen towards the forest. Abstract At the foundation of a species' vulnerability to climate change are the linkages between its physiological capacity, microclimate exposure and behavioural decision‐making. n4d5563dbf922: Leaves influence global climate and water resources by regulating the flows of CO2, energy and water between the atmosphere and land. n827795c57871: This study demonstrates that competition structures access to mutualistic partners that vary in value. Competitively dominant ants disproportionately invest in larger aphid colonies that produce more honeydew, restricting subordinate ants to smaller colonies. n53d9d47fc60e: Identifying the existence of ‘cryptic’ morphs is critical in animal ecology for providing a basis for accurately testing links between phenotype and environment. nff4c6d1fb11a: Using a multi‐decadal dataset, we show the relative influence of predator recovery, annual weather, density dependence, and anthropogenic top‐down forces on a large herbivore. n0cbeb77a9559: Food availability is crucial for alpine consumers during short growing seasons. n16f30d090c53: This study provides the first experimental test of alternative models explaining species–area relationships (SARs) in patches of the sabellariid tubeworm Sabellaria alveolata. The results indicate that faunal richness per unit area was independent of patch size, consistently with passive sampling theory, while other diversity indices highlighted the occurrence of size‐specific processes. These findings challenge the traditional view of SARs, suggesting the potential key role of mosaics of sabellariid patch sizes to maintain associated biodiversity and ecosystem function and the importance of incorporating within‐habitat factors when attempting to apply general ecological theories to conservation and management. Abstract The increase of species richness with the available or sampled area is a fundamental principle in ecology, but explanatory models of this relationship have never been tested in worm reefs representing priority systems as biodiversity hotspots and habitats of conservation concern. nad3ce441d643: Across an alpine grassland restoration sequence, stabilizing mechanisms shifted from asynchrony towards averaging. Community evenness increased, while averaging changed from destabilizing to stabilizing. Statistical mediation linked evenness to the dominance effect primarily through Taylor's scaling exponent. Abstract Maintaining temporal community stability during ecological restoration is essential for sustaining ecosystem services, yet how stabilizing pathways shift directionally across restoration stages remains poorly understood. These findings identify a management opportunity in mid-to-late restoration, during which promoting species evenness may strengthen the mechanisms underpinning long-term community stability. 摘要 在生态恢复过程中维持群落时间稳定性，对于持续提供生态系统服务至关重要，但稳定化途径如何随恢复阶段发生方向性转变，仍缺乏充分认识。本研究以青藏高原高寒草地为对象，在一个跨越 13 年的恢复序列中，考察了三种稳定化作用(优势度、异步性和平均化作用)的时间动态。 将纵向监测数据(第 1–5 年)与时空替代数据(第 6–13 年)相结合，在九个连续的五年滑动窗口中，将群落时间稳定性分解为优势度、异步性和平均化作用，并追踪其变化。采用线性混合效应模型分析群落均匀度、物种丰富度和稳定性的变化轨迹，并通过中介分析检验均匀度经由泰勒幂律指数 b 影响优势度作用的路径。 尽管物种丰富度下降，群落均匀度总体上升(R 2 = 0.834，p < 0.001)。沿恢复序列，稳定化途径的组成逐渐发生转变:早期以异步性作用为主，后期基于时空替代数据的窗口则以平均化作用为主。 值得注意的是，平均化作用在多样性较低时具有去稳定化效应(ω > 1)，随着群落发展转变为较强的稳定化作用。均匀度主要通过泰勒幂律指数 b 调节优势度作用，间接路径占总中介效应的大部分(Sobel 检验:Z = −4.54，p < 0.001)。 综合。 稳定化途径在恢复过程中依次发生转变，统计平均化在后期取代了基于异步性的稳定化作用。相较于净稳定性本身，稳定化机制组成的变化更能表征随着恢复进程推进，群落通过何种机制维持稳定。这些发现指出了恢复中后期的一个管理机会:提高物种均匀度可能增强支撑群落长期稳定性的机制。
n91fa8105dc87: The study demonstrates that the abiotic potential for treeline shift is nullified by the biotic collapse of critical facilitative recruitment niches. The current treeline represents a microclimatically modulated and biotically buffered optimum with no future analogue under climate warming. Abstract Predicting plant responses to climate change, such as shifting of mountain treelines, requires a mechanistic understanding of how abiotic and biotic factors interact to regulate tree regeneration. Although climate warming is anticipated to alleviate thermal constraints on tree growth beyond the current treeline limits, the interaction between biotic facilitation and climate in regulating tree regeneration remains poorly understood. In this study, we aimed to unravel the interactive role of microclimate, functional traits, soil properties and shrub facilitation on the recruitment of Himalayan birch tree, Betula utilis. For this, we combined controlled seed germination and seedling production with in‐situ transplant experiment at two sites along the treeline elevational gradient: below treeline (BTL), at treeline (TLN) and above treeline (ATL), supplemented with 3‐year field monitoring and multi‐driver modelling. We ran response‐surface and facilitation‐surface models to simulate the combined effects of soil warming and co‐varying environmental shifts on seedling survival and facilitation stability. The tree recruitment revealed a unimodal pattern, with both seed germination (23–31%) and seedling survival peaking at TLN. Seedling survival was predominantly dependent on biotic facilitation, with a 45% mean reduction in survival probability in open microsites compared to those beneath shrub canopies in TLN and ATL. Soil temperature emerged as the dominant abiotic driver, explaining 60–80% of the variation in modelled seedling survival. Our results reveal a novel warming‐facilitation paradox: while warming of +1.66°C could create thermal conditions in ATL analogous to the current optimum recruitment conditions of TLN, this same warming was predicted to cause a catastrophic decline in facilitation stability, with beneficial effects of shrubs rapidly reducing beyond a threshold of +1.5–1.7°C. Synthesis. Our findings demonstrate that the abiotic potential for treeline shift is nullified by the biotic collapse of critical facilitative recruitment niches. The current treeline represents a microclimatically modulated and biotically buffered optimum with no future analogue under climate warming. Our study provides a mechanistic explanation for widely reported treeline vegetation lag to climate and also posits that predictive models failing to incorporate the thermal sensitivity of biotic facilitation and its interaction with soil and resource‐acquisition strategies will overestimate climate warming‐induced treeline shifts.
n238f24b6e623: Medicinal plants face growing threats from climate change, habitat fragmentation, selective harvesting, and other human-induced pressures that may diminish genetic diversity and weaken evolutionary resilience. Recent studies in population genomics and landscape genomics indicate that resilience is influenced not just by diversity across a species, but also by how adaptive variation is distributed among populations and its connection to environmental gradients. In medicinal plants, factors such as geographic isolation, precipitation, temperature, salinity, and demographic history have been linked to population differentiation and potential adaptive loci. Genomic methods can thus shift conservation from outlining neutral diversity to pinpointing populations and alleles that may be significant for upcoming climates. Simultaneously, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and epigenetic research shows that genetic adaptation is enhanced by phenotypic plasticity and environmental modulation of stress and specialized metabolism pathways. Nevertheless, direct evidence linking adaptive genomic variation to fitness in wild medicinal plant populations is still scarce, and numerous at-risk taxa are deficient in genomic resources. In this study, we integrate recent findings that connect genetic variability, regional adaptation, molecular stress responses, and conservation strategies for medicinal plants. We emphasize landscape genomics and genomic vulnerability as tangible connections between evolutionary ecology and conservation, stressing the importance of incorporating adaptive variation, epigenetic plasticity, demographic history, ecological interactions, and habitat preservation. Future research should emphasize non-model medicinal species, wider geographic sampling, temporal genomic tracking, and field validation of potential adaptive loci.
ne828877f222b: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Plant litter input can affect soil organic carbon (SOC) decomposition, that is the priming effect. Variation in experimental conditions, litter characteristics and soil properties among individual studies has led to inconsistent reports of priming effects. We aimed to synthesize global patterns and drivers of the litter‐induced priming effect. Microbial biomass C also increased by an average of 45% following litter addition, with a greater increase under stem litter than under other litter types, consistent with the microbial N‐mining hypothesis. Experimental conditions, including incubation duration and litter addition rate, were more important in explaining priming induced by leaf and stem litter, whereas litter characteristics and soil properties, such as C:N ratio and pH, were more important in explaining root litter‐induced priming, potentially reflecting the relatively high recalcitrance of root litter. Furthermore, the effects of soil properties on the priming effect depended on litter characteristics, with particularly strong interactions observed for root litter, highlighting that root litter‐induced priming is jointly regulated by litter quality and the soil properties. We emphasize the importance of the specificity of litter type in regulating the priming effect. Future studies should comprehensively investigate litter characteristics and their interactions with experimental conditions and soil properties using long‐term experiments to improve global predictions of SOC decomposition via the priming effect. Abstract Soil salinization and alkalization often suppress microbial functional activity, triggering negative feedback loops in microbial metabolism, degrading nutrients and agricultural productivity. However, the impacts of saline versus alkaline soils on microbial metabolism remain unclear. However, the two regional soil systems showed divergent nutrient limitation patterns associated with contrasting physicochemical and microbial conditions. Saline soils exhibited acute microbial N limitation (VTN/P limitation = −6.51), which was associated with lower N availability, including 53.29% lower DTN than in alkaline soils, macroaggregate-associated N depletion, and bacterial-associated network reorganization. Microbial functional profiles further indicated greater genetic potential for denitrification and lower genetic potential for dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium, with A 1 soils having 25.12% lower nirK/S abundance and 49.68% higher napA abundance than S 1 soils.
